Under the reported chronological evaluation procedure, the model achieved a precision of 0.7320, recall of 0.4956, F1-score of 0.5910 and area under the precision–recall curve of 0.5984 at a decision threshold of 0.5350. These results indicate moderate fraud-discrimination performance, although approximately half of the labelled fraudulent cases were not detected at the selected threshold. Further evaluation against established baseline models, independent validation of cryptocurrency fraud labels and experimental assessment of the proposed blockchain subsystem are necessary to establish the framework's comparative effectiveness and operational suitability.

all.title: Smart Commerce Fraud Detection Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Smart commerce platforms increasingly depend on digital identities, online payments, user reviews, and high-volume order processing, creating multiple opportunities for fraudulent activity. Existing rule-based mechanisms are transparent and easy to implement, but they are static, require frequent manual updates, and can generate false positives when fraud behaviour changes. This paper proposes a smart-commerce fraud detection framework that combines transactional, behavioural, contextual, and review-related signals within a unified artificial intelligence and machine-learning pipeline. The proposed framework uses supervised learning models such as Random Forest and XGBoost for labelled transaction and account classification, Isolation Forest for anomaly detection, and an optional natural-language processing layer for suspicious review identification. Behavioural features include login frequency, transaction velocity, device usage, location consistency, order cancellation rate, address changes, payment method, and review activity. The system incorporates class-imbalance handling, feature engineering, real-time risk scoring, and an explainability layer based on feature importance and SHAP/LIME-style local explanations. The design also supports continuous feedback and future graph-based analysis for coordinated fraud networks. Its methodology covers data acquisition, inspection, preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, model selection, prediction, explanation, and deployment. A risk score combines supervised transaction-fraud probability, anomaly score, behavioural risk, contextual inconsistency, and review/account risk. Events are assigned low-, medium-, or high-risk states to support normal processing, additional verification, or blocking/manual review. Evaluation is planned using precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, confusion matrix, false-positive rate, and inference time. The paper focuses on a reproducible research framework and does not fabricate experimental performance values; numerical results are to be reported after implementation on the final project dataset. The proposed architecture is intended to improve early fraud detection, reduce false positives, strengthen transaction security, and increase trust in smart-commerce platforms.

all.title: Maturity-Aware Dual-Timescale Replay for Delayed-Feedback Financial Fraud Screening
all.venue: International Journal of World Economic Research
all.abstract: Fraud-screening labels often arrive after a transaction, with fraudulent outcomes confirmed later than legitimate outcomes. This class-dependent observation process distorts conventional replay under concept drift. We instantiate the adaptive recent/global prioritized replay of DriftShield in a one-step cost-sensitive fraud controller, and extend it with maturity-gated access, transaction-time recency and capped inverse confirmation-visibility weighting. A second, arrival-driven scorer supplies a faster adaptation channel; its predictions are combined with the slow replay scorer using a fixed mixture. The system is tested prequentially on an explicitly synthetic 42,000-event stream with two changes in fraud signatures and asymmetric reporting delays. In the three-seed comparison, 42 model/delay runs include three component ablations and two stress-test delays. An additional 12-seed paired evaluation reports F1 0.262 and average precision 0.236 for the dual-timescale controller, versus 0.239 and 0.223 for arrival-time replay. A fast-only scorer with the same threshold controller instead reaches F1 0.265 and average precision 0.242: the slow branch does not improve that stronger comparator in this simulator. Paired intervals and a future-label nonanticipation test delimit the reproducible benefits of maturity-aware replay without implying production deployment gains.

all.title: Leakage-aware federated-style simulation for fraud risk prediction in AI-enabled FinTech platforms
all.abstract: AI-enabled FinTech platforms increasingly rely on automated fraud-risk prediction to secure high-volume digital payments, mobile-money transactions, and real-time financial services. However, fraud detection remains difficult because fraudulent transactions are rare, financial data are sensitive, and centralized machine-learning models may create privacy and data-governance risks. This study evaluates a leakage-aware and imbalance-aware federated-style simulation for fraud-risk prediction in AI-enabled FinTech platforms. The study does not implement FedAvg, cryptographic secure aggregation, differential privacy, or model-parameter exchange. Instead, the PaySim Synthetic Financial Dataset was partitioned into five simulated FinTech clients, local models were trained separately, and prediction-level aggregation was used to compare centralized and simulated decentralized learning settings. The experimental workflow included data-quality assessment, leakage-aware feature selection, feature engineering, class-imbalance analysis, centralized model development, threshold optimization, and federated-style model comparison. The results show that fraud cases represented only 0.0466% of all transactions and occurred only in CASH_OUT and TRANSFER operations. The best-balanced centralized model was the Improved Random Forest at a threshold of 0.33, achieving an F1-score of 0.3019. Federated Ensemble Aggregation achieved the highest PR-AUC of 0.2699 and a precision of 1.0000, but its recall remained low at 0.1429. The centralized Improved Random Forest retained the highest F1-score of 0.3019, indicating a stronger overall precision-recall balance. Global feature-importance analysis showed that transaction amount, log-transformed amount, temporal features, transaction type, and destination-account activity were the main fraud-risk indicators. These findings should be interpreted as evidence from simulated decentralized fraud-risk learning rather than a full secure federated learning implementation.

all.title: Developing an Improved Hybrid Framework for Detecting Financial Fraud using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models under Imbalanced Data Conditions
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Financial fraud detection has become increasingly challenging due to the rapid growth of digital transactions and the highly imbalanced nature of financial datasets. Traditional detection techniques often fail to identify fraudulent activities because legitimate transactions significantly outnumber fraudulent ones. This study proposes an integrated hybrid framework that combines machine learning and deep learning techniques to improve fraud identification and classification. The framework incorporates Random Forest and Gradient Boosting algorithms alongside advanced deep learning architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) networks. To address class imbalance, specialized data-resampling methods and cost-sensitive learning strategies are employed. Furthermore, an ensemble-based meta-learning mechanism integrates the prediction outputs of individual models to enhance overall classification performance. Experimental findings indicate that the proposed hybrid approach achieves better accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score than the individual baseline models. The framework offers a promising approach for reliable financial fraud detection under highly imbalanced data conditions.

all.title: Product scope, product switching, and ownership structure
all.abstract: We use comprehensive trademark data to investigate how ownership structure relates to firm product scope and product-switching behavior. We find that higher institutional ownership is associated with more active resource reallocation within firms through more frequent product additions and removals. The net effect of these additions and removals expands overall product scope. The evidence is consistent with the career-concerns channel, in which institutional monitoring insulates managers from short-term performance fluctuations arising from product-market changes. We also examine common ownership across rival firms. The results indicate that common ownership facilitates technological-spillover internalization rather than anticompetitive product pruning.

all.title: Heterogeneous Responses to Monetary Policy: The role of Floating Rate Loans
all.abstract: This study examines the floating rate channel —a mechanism through which monetary policy affects firms’ investment and credit demand based on their exposure to variable rate loans. Using a granular loan-level dataset from the euro area, we find that firms with variable rate loans significantly reduce their borrowing after monetary tightening, compared to firms with fixed rate loans. This effect is most pronounced among the smallest firms, consistent with the theoretical view that the floating rate channel is explained by financial constraints. Our results highlight the heterogeneity in firms’ reactions to interest rate changes and underscore the importance of accounting for firm size and financial constraints in monetary policy analysis. JEL codes: G21, G30, E52

all.title: SEAL: An integral methodology for evaluating the security of agentic LLMs
all.abstract: The adoption of large language models (LLMs) as agentic systems introduces security risks that extend beyond traditional prompt-based interactions. This paper presents SEAL , an integral methodology for generating adversarial evaluation datasets and benchmarking the security of LLMs with tool-calling capabilities. Our methodology integrates automated red teaming through PyRIT for adversarial prompt generation and Promptfoo for structured benchmarking under controlled inference-time settings, without requiring training-time modifications or external guardrails, providing a unified evaluation workflow. The evaluation covers three adversarial strategies intended to measure confidentiality, integrity, and availability: direct tool injection, system prompt exfiltration, and indirect prompt injection with semantic denial-of-service (SDoS) effects. We further assess a semantic defense-in-depth strategy based on progressively hardened system prompts. Through extensive experimentation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of SEAL for intrinsic security evaluation of agentic LLMs. Across the evaluated models, several commercial and larger open-source systems tend to exhibit greater security stability in specific dimensions, although this pattern is not uniform across all evaluated models and attack strategies. A more consistent finding is a critical trade-off between robustness and operational availability.

all.title: Graph-theoretic multi-view feature engineering for interpretable BGP Anomaly detection
all.abstract: Graph-based and flat statistical feature spaces are both used for operational anomaly detection, yet how complementary they are—and how well detectors built on them transfer across deployments—remains largely untested. We study both questions for Internet inter-domain routing (BGP). We combine a graph-topological view and a statistical view in a multi-view detector and evaluate cross-domain transfer with a factorial design (two autonomous systems, two route collectors) and CORAL domain adaptation over 12 directed transfer pairs. A complementarity analysis confirms that the two views carry predominantly orthogonal signals, motivating their fusion, whose benefit is then verified by a single-view-versus-fusion ablation. Our central finding is that transfer difficulty is driven by topology asymmetry, not observation-point distance: detection holds within a single AS (macro-F1 up to 0.878) but collapses across structurally different ASes (0.40–0.70). This yields a topology-driven model-selection hypothesis—flat classifiers (MLP) for sparse, hierarchical ASes and message-passing graph networks (TopoGPS) for dense peering meshes—paired with per-detection feature attribution for interpretability. On the April 2025 Iberian power outage, it reaches 75% recall at a 1.3% false-alarm rate. The analysis methodology —not a single trained model—targets other domains that pair relational graphs with event streams.

all.title: A foundation-model-based expert perception system for reliable decision support in automated intralogistics
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming a fundamental enabling technology for intelligent industrial systems in which autonomous perception supports operational decision making. Automated warehouses increasingly rely on visual information to coordinate robotic manipulation, inventory supervision, navigation, safety monitoring, and exception management. However, practical deployment remains challenging because industrial environments exhibit dense object arrangements, repeated visual patterns, partial occlusions, scale variation, and strict confidence policies intended to minimize erroneous operational interventions. Under these conditions, conventional object detection metrics alone provide only a partial characterization of the reliability required by downstream decision-support modules. This work presents an applied expert perception methodology that adapts DINOv3 feature representations with the proposal-based localization mechanism of Faster R-CNN for automated intralogistics. Rather than introducing a novel neural network topology, this work formulates static detection confidence thresholds as explicit operational decision policies and establishes a deployment-oriented execution pipeline. We investigate a progressive unfreezing strategy for adapting self-supervised representations to industrial domain data while limiting abrupt modifications of the pretrained backbone. Furthermore, we address the dynamic graph execution overhead of two-stage ViT detectors through a hybrid BFloat16 and TensorRT optimization strategy on edge-proxy hardware. Experimental evaluations show that the integrated pipeline achieves competitive object detection in challenging industrial scenes while providing real-time model inference on the evaluated NVIDIA L4 edge-proxy platform. The proposed system is evaluated on the Logistics Objects in Context (LOCO) dataset and the Safe Human 17 (SH17) dataset, representing complementary warehouse logistics and industrial safety scenarios. Comparative experiments against YOLOv11 analyze conventional detection performance together with threshold-dependent behavior, localization capability, operational reliability, and computational efficiency under realistic deployment conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture consistently preserves a larger proportion of its detection capability under increasingly restrictive confidence policies, particularly in dense and partially occluded environments. Furthermore, TensorRT optimization reduces inference latency to 21.90 ms per image, corresponding to approximately 45 frames per second on an NVIDIA L4 GPU without significant degradation in predictive performance. The results indicate that combining foundation-model representations, proposal-based localization, progressive domain adaptation, and deployment-oriented optimization provides an effective strategy for developing expert perception systems capable of supplying reliable visual evidence for intelligent industrial decision-support applications.

all.title: Adversarial examples beyond spurious features: An experimental study
institutions: Universitatea Națională de Știință și Tehnologie Politehnica București
all.abstract: Spurious correlations — non-causal associations between superficial attributes and target labels — fundamentally compromise the reliability of machine learning models, creating deceptive performance that breaks down under data distribution shifts. Prior research links these features to adversarial vulnerabilities exploited by gradient-based evasion attacks. This study investigates spurious correlations through a security lens by proposing two spurious-free gradient-based evasion attacks targeting neural networks that rely on non-essential features. Their design rests on two assumptions: 1) biased gradients towards simple features, and 2) overconfident output probabilities. We examine both defender and attacker perspectives — emphasizing mitigation via data pre-processing or robust learning, while also evaluating attack effectiveness when spurious features have been reduced or eliminated. We assess our attacks on benchmark vision datasets against standard neural networks and established spurious-robust techniques. Results show that our attacks successfully diminish the influence of spurious attributes, with each attack performing best in specific scenarios. Our findings underscore that no universally applicable security evaluation can fully counteract spurious attributes, and that focusing on causal relationships is essential for building more rigorous robustness assessment tools.

all.title: Inferring health motivation from wearable data: A cluster-based approach to predicting healthcare claims
all.abstract: Understanding what drives individuals to maintain health behaviours is crucial for designing effective interventions and accurately predicting healthcare outcomes. This study introduces a novel method for inferring motivational states from wearable exercise data, leveraging self-determination theory to interpret latent behavioural patterns. Using longitudinal data from 15,904 participants in a gamified health programme, behavioural patterns are profiled into motivation-informed categories, amotivation, controlled motivation and autonomous motivation, which are then incorporated into predictive models of healthcare claims. Post-analysis reveals that these profiles align with theoretical constructs and enhance the model's sensitivity to at-risk individuals, consequently improving recall and F1 scores. Explainable machine learning techniques highlight the predictive significance of motivation alongside conventional clinical indicators. This approach bridges psychological theory and data science, offering scalable, interpretable insights for insurers, clinicians and digital health interventions aiming to personalise care and optimise outcomes, while providing an empirical foundation for the future validation of the profiles.

all.title: Uncertainty-aware conformal prediction of compressive strength in low-carbon UHPC: Framework development and experimental validation
all.abstract: UHPC offers exceptionally high compressive strength but carries a heavy embodied-carbon footprint due to its elevated cement content, motivating the use of SCMs, including fly ash, silica fume, and GGBFS as partial cement replacements. However, accurate prediction remains challenging due to complex nonlinear interactions among the mixture constituents, fibre properties, curing conditions, and specimen geometry. Although existing ML studies capture these coupled effects and provide deterministic predictions, they often overlook uncertainty and heteroscedastic variability, leaving their reliability untested. This study developed an uncertainty-aware ML framework, using a harmonized database of 2,032 low-carbon UHPC mixtures incorporating one or more of FA, SF, and GGBFS, to predict compressive strength (23.6–––298 MPa) across curing ages of 1 to 90 days. Among six evaluated ML models (RF, XGBoost, AdaBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and ANN), LightGBM achieved the highest accuracy with R 2 = 0.945 and RMSE = 9.41 MPa. Prediction uncertainty was quantified by integrating six conformal prediction methods with each model and evaluating 36 ML–CP combinations using EC, MIW, AIS, and ES. Among all combinations, LightGBM–Jackknife achieved the best uncertainty-aware performance, providing a strong balance between accuracy and interval quality (EC = 0.959, MIW = 33.3 MPa, AIS = 38.49 MPa, and ES = 0.753). Experimental validation on five binary and ternary mixes at 14 and 28 days returned full interval coverage at both ages, with mean errors of 6.81% and 1.52% and mean interval widths of 21.96 MPa and 20.39 MPa, respectively, demonstrating the direct applicability of the proposed framework for low-carbon UHPC mix design within the validated domain of compressive strength ≥ 60 MPa.

all.title: Managing disruption in dynamic three-echelon healthcare supply chains using an integrated machine learning and optimization model: A case study of the insulin supply chain
all.abstract: Healthcare supply chains operating in dynamic and disruption prone environments face several fundamental challenges. Static decision making under uncertainty often proves ineffective, critical resources may be poorly allocated when disruptions are likely, and the rapid growth of possible scenarios leads to high computational complexity. To address these issues, this study proposes an innovative disruption management approach, Machine Learning-based Real-time Optimization for Disruptions (ML-ROD), which combines machine learning and optimization to support proactive decision making. The proposed ML-ROD approach first employs a machine learning model trained on historical data to predict the failure probabilities of network links. It then applies an optimization-based mechanism to identify and prioritize critical connections, thereby reducing the overall scenario space. Finally, the model dynamically selects the most appropriate resilience strategies and reallocates resources in each planning period. The results show that, compared with the historical-average baseline, the real-time ML-ROD implementation reduces operational costs by 17% and carbon emissions by 13%. Against the K-Medoids distance-based clustering benchmark, both methods were supplied with the same predicted link-failure probabilities. ML-ROD reduced cost by 10% and emissions by 5% under accurate prediction and retained cost and emission advantages under inaccurate predictions, while unmet insulin demand was tracked as a service-level outcome. Carbon-emission performance was strategy-dependent, with K-Medoids performing better under emergency procurement alone. Robustness tests further showed that these advantages persist up to the tested 20% prediction-error threshold.

all.title: DOiT: Better Money-Flow Ranking Can Coexist with Worse Account Selection in Anti-Money Laundering Review
all.abstract: Anti-money laundering (AML) review selects suspicious accounts and reconstructs transfers. Downstream graph neural networks (GNNs) rank money-flow evidence but may also reorder the account queue. DOiT separates these decisions at equal review capacity: account selection determines where graph investigation starts. Across AMLWorld and AMLNet, GNN reordering harms higher-yield upstream orders but helps lower-yield ones. On AMLWorld, this harm coexists with higher transaction average precision (AP) in dimension-matched, per-run decoders, demonstrating separable ranking abilities. At small capacities, positive neighbors can displace a denser upstream prefix and lower yield; replacement costs fall as that prefix is exhausted, allowing the preferred order to reverse. A restricted-access synthetic benchmark informed by real transaction patterns reproduces this separation and validation-based upstream preservation. Capacity-matched combination protects upstream ordering while retaining GNN money-flow analysis, admitting GNN queue influence only where held-out evidence supports it.

all.title: JEV vs. LLMs: A Comparative Analysis for Phishing Email Detection
all.abstract: Phishing remains a major source of credential theft and fraudulent payments, and email security systems must classify large message volumes reliably, quickly, and at manageable cost. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer flexible text understanding, but their token-based generation increases response time and API cost, and the reliability of their confidence values requires measurement. Jev 1.13, a typed decision model from TypeSafe AI, instead returns a structured outcome with a confidence value. This paper compares Jev 1.13 with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Meta Llama 4 Maverick on a labelled dataset of 1500 emails, covering classification performance, decision latency, token consumption, API cost, and probability calibration. Jev achieves the highest accuracy (79.67%), precision (71.43%), recall (97.97%), and F1 score (82.62%). It also records the shortest batch time (173.88 seconds), the lowest token count (597,895), the lowest cost (USD 0.015103 per 1000 decisions), and the lowest Brier score (0.1698) and ECE (0.1594). These results suggest that Jev is a promising option for fast, structured, high-volume triage. LLMs retain the advantage of generating explanations, which we do not evaluate, and all four systems require further validation before standalone deployment.

all.title: Large Payments Model
all.abstract: Payment applications such as fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization draw on overlapping transaction information. This motivates a reusable payments intelligence layer that shares learned representations and predictive signals, rather than developing predictive models independently for each task. Realizing this shared capability requires handling heterogeneous transaction fields, high-cardinality identifiers, lifecycle-dependent attributes, long histories, and rare outcomes while meeting latency and cost constraints. We present Large Payments Model (LPM), a domain-specific foundation model designed for operational use and trained from scratch on large-scale structured transaction data to learn reusable representations for payment prediction tasks. LPM employs field-specific encodings and lifecycle-aware self-supervision in two complementary architectures: the Independent variant uses hybrid masking and supports efficient per-transaction inference, while the Sequence variant incorporates entity-linked histories through compact latent representations for richer temporal context. Optional distillation enables resource-constrained deployment. We pretrain LPM on up to 400 billion tokens and study scaling, downstream performance, and representation reuse. LPM improves over strong task-specific baselines across multiple prediction tasks in Merchant and Treasury Services, demonstrating applicability in distinct payment domains. Its representations also facilitate adaptation to a target not observed during pretraining through compact task-specific components. Together with production deployment, these results position LPM as a practical basis for reusable payments intelligence.

all.title: Social Engineering Attack Detection in Corporate Communications
all.abstract: Social Engineering attacks continue to pose a significant risk to the corporate world with a growing level of sophistication. It is difficult to distinguish between authentic and phishing communication via email, chat, and phone. They pose a risk of exposing trade secrets and confidential communications and can create a chain of attack from lower-level employees up to executives. Therefore, we study this growing threat using real-world datasets to build baseline machine-learning models. Our TF-IDF models classify emails as phishing or safe, achieving accuracy above 90%. We build on this by exploring whether psychological manipulation and persuasion indicators can be measured to play a significant role in detecting phishing. Instead of relying solely on surface-level lexical features, we derive interpretable lexicon-based indicators of urgency, trust, greed, and other persuasion cues from the combined email dataset. By evaluating these manipulation-oriented features on their own, we measure how much signal they carry (ROC-AUC of 0.74 on a held-out test split) and test whether they transfer to held-out email sources.

all.title: Diretor de Regulação do BC dará entrevista coletiva às 11 horas de quinta-feira (26/11) sobre as medidas que tratam dos riscos associados ao endividamento de famílias e empresas
all.abstract: ​O diretor de Regulação do Banco Central (BC), Gilneu Vivan, dará uma entrevista coletiva às 11 horas de amanhã (26/11) sobre as medidas para lidar com os riscos associados ao endividamento de famílias e empresas aprovadas pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional e o BC. A coletiva será realizada na Sala de Entrevistas localizada no 2º Subsolo do Edifício-Sede do Banco Central, em Brasília. A entrevista poderá ser acompanhada em tempo real pelo Canal do Banco Central no YouTube . Os jornalistas interessados em participar presencialmente da coletiva precisarão apenas se identificar na recepção do Edifício-Sede do Banco Central. Os profissionais de imprensa poderão fazer perguntas apenas presencialmente, não serão admitidas questões feitas por meio virtual. Com isso, a entrevista coletiva do chefe do Departamento de Estatísticas do Banco Central, Fernando Rocha, sobre as estatísticas do setor externo de outubro passará das 10h30 para as 15 horas. A publicação das estatísticas do setor externo será feita no horário de praxe, às 8h30 de quinta-feira.

all.title: BC aperfeiçoa norma sobre a participação em operações no mercado aberto
all.abstract: ​O Banco Central (BC) aprovou alterações normativas com o objetivo de ampliar a participação de instituições financeiras nas operações do BC e para atualizar procedimentos operacionais do Sistema Especial de Liquidação e de Custódia (Selic). Entre as mudanças está a criação de um procedimento facultativo para readequação dos valores financeiros de operações compromissadas com livre movimentação dos títulos realizadas pelo BC. O mecanismo permitirá que, em condições previamente definidas, seja promovido o realinhamento entre o valor da operação e o valor de mercado dos títulos envolvidos, o que contribuirá para a participação de um maior número de instituições nesse instrumento. A norma também prevê a ampliação do acesso aos depósitos voluntários a prazo mantidos no BC. As instituições financeiras não liquidantes no Selic, como cooperativas de crédito, poderão utilizar diretamente esse instrumento para aplicação de recursos, por intermédio de seus liquidantes-padrão. A medida visa contribuir para uma gestão mais eficiente da liquidez pelas instituições financeiras por meio desse instrumento complementar de atuação no mercado aberto. Adicionalmente, o BC fez ajustes operacionais e a atualização de procedimentos e nomenclaturas no Regulamento do Selic, com foco em maior automação, segurança operacional e alinhamento às práticas operacionais atualmente adotadas pelo mercado financeiro. all.title: FEDS Paper: Artificial Intelligence and the U.S. Economy: Current Evidence
all.abstract: Nick Carollo , Leland D. Crane , Daniel Garcia Molina , and Joseph Nichols We assess the current evidence on how AI-related investment and the use of AI are affecting the U.S. macroeconomy. Specifically, we document the boom in data center capital investment, the current rate of adoption of AI tools in the economy, the impact of the AI-related investment surge on prices, and discuss whether AI tools have affected the labor market and productivity yet. Driven by current and expected future demand for AI services, investment in data centers, both the physical structures and semiconductor chips and other IT equipment inside the structures, has climbed sharply. AI adoption is growing rapidly both among consumers and firms, though most firms are currently not using AI very intensively or at all. AI model-producing firms have also grown extremely fast, and now account for a noticeable fraction of software industry gross output. Prices have climbed in sectors that provide direct inputs to the data centers, such as memory chips. Effects on the labor market so far appear small and somewhat mixed. Similarly, the effects of AI on aggregate productivity growth also appear to be small so far, and the recent pickup in productivity likely reflects factors that predated the diffusion on generative AI.

all.title: Geordie Shore star and illegal finfluencer sentenced for promoting high-risk investments on social media
all.abstract: Aaron Chalmers, a reality TV star and social media content creator, and finfluencer Jason Agbodza have been sentenced for illegally promoting an unauthorised foreign exchange trading scheme on social media. Chalmers, 39 and from Newcastle, was sentenced at City of London Magistrates Court. He previously pleaded guilty and today (19 November) was fined £3,072 and ordered to pay costs of £2,836.Having risen to fame on Geordie Shore, Chalmers has more than 2 million followers on Instagram. Agbodza, 35, of London, was also fined £1,173 and ordered to pay costs of £2,114 after pleading guilty.Both men encouraged followers to invest in foreign exchange (forex or FX) trading through contracts for difference (CFDs), without being authorised to promote them. CFDs are high-risk derivatives, and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has previously found that approximately 80% of customers lose money when investing in them.Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market integrity at the FCA, said:'With more than two million Instagram followers, Chalmers exploited his online influence to illegally promote investments to a vast audience. Agbodza made significant profits from an unlawful investment scheme. These cases send a clear message: we will take decisive action against those that break the law and put consumers at risk.'Separately, earlier this year the FCA issued cautions to 2 individuals for posting illegal financial promotions on social media. The cautions will appe

all.title: Decoding the cyber-AI nexus
all.abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the cyber threat landscape, with significant implications for financial stability in the euro area. This special feature explores the complex interplay between AI and cybersecurity, highlighting how advanced AI models are enabling attackers and defenders alike to enhance their capabilities. Highly capable and agentic AI systems are increasing the scale, speed and sophistication of attacks while also introducing new vulnerabilities. These include AI models themselves being exposed to novel types of attack and AI agents failing to act as their human operators intend. Critically, new AI capabilities could favour attackers, as the availability of low-cost AI agents lowers entry barriers. Meanwhile defenders remain constrained by the cost of deploying frontier models, governance challenges and slower, regulation-bound decision-making. This leaves defenders structurally disadvantaged, at least in the near term. Euro area banks, despite their high level of cybersecurity maturity, face asymmetries in access to cutting-edge AI models and rely heavily on concentrated third-party providers. This increases the risk of systemic disruption, as AI adoption transforms the channels through which cyber incidents propagate. Mitigating these risks requires banks, AI developers, cybersecurity firms and regulators to coordinate their efforts to enhance resilience, improve governance and address emerging systemic vulnerabilities.

all.title: Artificial intelligence and European firms: the cost of market-based financing
all.abstract: This box examines how exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) is reflected in the market-based financing conditions of European firms. Using a novel firm-level measure of AI exposure derived from the earnings call transcripts of STOXX Europe 600 constituents, we show that AI exposure extends beyond a narrow set of infrastructure providers and hyperscalers, encompassing a broader range of firms that adopt AI for product innovation or productivity gains. Panel regressions show that AI-exposed firms earn a robust equity return premium of around 1.3 percentage points per quarter and pay significantly lower option-adjusted spreads on their corporate bonds, while also issuing a relatively higher share of long-dated debt. These patterns indicate that AI exposure is priced into both equity and corporate bond markets across the wider economy in Europe and is more broadly distributed than the concentrated market rally would imply.

all.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
all.abstract: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

all.title: Financial statement fraud detection under delayed regulatory labels: A semi-supervised BiGAN framework
Modeling the Future of Finance: Digital Transformation, Fintech Innovations, Market Adaptation, and Strategic Growth
all.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
all.abstract: The financial industry is undergoing a profound transformation driven by rapid advancements in digital technologies, fintech innovations, and evolving market dynamics. This paper explores the critical role of digital transformation in reshaping financial services, emphasizing the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, big data analytics, and cloud computing to enhance efficiency, security, and customer experience. Fintech innovations have disrupted traditional banking models, enabling digital payments, decentralized finance (DeFi), roboadvisors, and open banking, fostering financial inclusion and accessibility. Market adaptation remains a crucial aspect of this evolution, as financial institutions must navigate regulatory challenges, cybersecurity threats, and shifting consumer expectations. This study examines the impact of digital disruption on traditional financial frameworks, highlighting the adoption of agile methodologies, risk management strategies, and regulatory compliance to ensure stability and resilience in a rapidly changing landscape. Additionally, the rise of embedded finance and digital currencies is reshaping transactional ecosystems, prompting financial institutions to innovate and collaborate with technology providers to sustain competitive advantage. Strategic growth in the digital finance era requires a data-driven approach, leveraging predictive analytics and machine learning to optimize investment decisions, enhance fraud detection, and personalize financial services. The paper presents a framework for financial organizations to embrace digital transformation by integrating emerging technologies with sustainable business models. Furthermore, it discusses the role of financial literacy and digital accessibility in fostering inclusive economic growth, ensuring that technological advancements benefit diverse populations. By synthesizing insights from case studies, market trends, and regulatory developments, this research provides a comprehensive outlook on the future of finance, highlighting opportunities for stakeholders to capitalize on technological advancements while mitigating associated risks. The study underscores the need for a collaborative approach among financial institutions, regulators, and technology firms to create a secure, efficient, and customer-centric financial ecosystem. The findings offer valuable implications for policymakers, industry leaders, and researchers seeking to understand and shape the trajectory of digital finance in the coming decades.

all.title: Machine Learning for Fraud Detection and Prevention in Forensic Accounting and Sustainable Reporting
all.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
all.abstract: Fraud detection in financial institutions has evolved into a highly challenging problem owing to the exponential increase in digital transactions, the complexities involved in data analysis, and the dynamic nature of fraud. Classical algorithms often lack efficiency while dealing with large volumes of dynamic data. In this chapter, a hybrid machine learning architecture has been proposed by integrating random forest and extreme gradient boosting using a weight-based fusion technique. The approach includes several steps such as data pre-processing, feature generation, and balancing the data distribution with SMOTE. Simulation results reveal that the proposed model yields an accuracy of 97.7% compared to other models concerning precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The approach facilitates forensic accounting as well as environmental, social, and governance-oriented sustainability reporting through better financial transparency, data integrity, and governance. The paper contributes to an efficient detection of financial fraud within intelligent financial ecosystems.

all.title: Privacy-Preserving AI in Finance: Federated Learning, Secure Computation, and GDPR Compliance for Fraud Detection and Credit Scoring
all.abstract: Financial institutions need large datasets to build AI systems, yet they must protect sensitive customer information under regimes such as the GDPR. This review examines how federated learning, secure multi-party computation, homomorphic encryption, and differential privacy support privacy-preserving AI in financial services. It covers the principles of data sovereignty, federated architectures for enterprise systems, and applications in cross-institutional collaboration, fraud detection, credit scoring, and personalized banking. It also discusses regulatory compliance, auditability, adversarial robustness, and cyber resilience. The literature indicates that these techniques help institutions meet data minimization requirements, reduce legal risk, and collaborate across borders. Trade-offs remain in computational overhead, latency, non-IID data, and model bias. Future work should focus on standardized protocols, hybrid privacy models, and auditing frameworks.

all.title: How Firm Is an AI Verdict in Finance? A Firm or Not-Firm Reading for Banks, Insurers and Stock Markets
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: AI programs now give a score for almost every decision in finance: a loan, a card or UPI payment, a name checked against a sanctions list, an insurance claim, a trading signal, a suspicious-trade alert. Each case gets one score from one pass, and nobody is told how firm that score is. This note describes a simple check that sits on top of any such AI program. The data arrives already processed, as a credit report, a payment record or a price feed, and it stays fixed (a machine of the second kind). The controller takes three to four setting vectors of the AI program's own non-learned settings, which the maker has already validated. For each setting value it sets X, a little below X and a little above X, and runs the same processed data each time. If the scores stay together, the verdict is firm. If they spread out, it depends on a setting. A computer-decided shunting action then moves along the validated setting vectors to one where the verdict is firm. Only if none is firm does that case go to the front of the human check list, while all other cases carry on. The learned weights, the data and the final cutoff are never changed. This is different from Lean proof checking, which proves that an action or a statement follows from rules written in advance. The firm score checks no rules. It tells how steady an AI program's own score is when its non-learned settings are moved, and a bank can use both together. The note covers six fields: loans and credit cards, card and UPI fraud, anti-money-laundering and KYC, insurance, trading signals, and exchange surveillance. Each field has a table of related work and how this method differs, and there is a plain explanation of how it differs from Bayesian networks and Monte Carlo dropout. Patent pending. Keywords firm or not-firm verdict, machine of the second kind, non-learned settings, spread of scores, shunting action, controller, setting vectors, Lean proof checking, banking AI, credit scoring, fraud detection, anti-money-laundering, insurance, trading signals, market surveillance, model risk
