all.title: A Selective State-Space Model for Real-Time E-Commerce Transaction Anomaly Detection in Management Information Systems
all.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
all.abstract: Management information systems (MISs) are subject to complex patterns of fraud, which change over time, as they occur at high speeds in class-imbalanced data streams. E-commerce platforms process very large transaction volumes. Existing detectors have three structural problems. The quadratic complexity of transformer attention makes it difficult to meet millisecond-scale inference budgets, recurrent models suffer from gradient pathologies over long behavioral sequences, and static loss functions are unable to adjust to the severe and changing class imbalance found in real transaction logs. This article introduces a selective state-space framework (SHOPMAMBA-MIS) that tackles all three challenges within a single framework. SHOPMAMBA-MIS consists of three parts: Selective-State Autoencoder (SSAE) to compress behavioral transaction sequences with linear-time selectivity, Transaction Attention Module (TAM) to emphasize anomaly boundaries per token without complete self-attention, and Dynamic Imbalance-Focal Sampler (DIFS) to dynamically sample the focal loss weight per mini-batch based on an exponential moving average (EMA) class-ratio estimator. On three public benchmarks, IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection, PaySim, and ULB Credit Card Fraud, SHOPMAMBA-MIS outperforms the best transformer baseline by +4.2 percentage points (F1), +5.9 percentage points (F1), and +4.1 percentage points (F1), respectively, while on the same benchmarks, its inference latency is reduced to 1.8 ms per transaction batch, which is 6.3 times faster than the slowest transformer baseline, TranAD (11.3 ms per batch), and its detection recall is kept above 92.8% (over 97.9% on IECIS and ULB) in all three benchmarks at a false-positive rate below 0.5%. The results obtained demonstrate the feasibility of the SHOPMAMBA-MIS, which can be implemented as an intelligent component in enterprise Management Information Systems, for real-time monitoring, enterprise control, and managerial decision-making in an enterprise. The framework is specifically suited to payment authorization pipelines that provide behavioral features (including rolling account-level aggregates where identifiers exist) and at least L prior transactions of history, exhibit intra-day fraud-rate variation, and enforce synchronous millisecond-scale latency constraints; applicability conditions and boundary cases.

all.title: From Batch to Instant: A Reference Architecture and Process Model for Modernizing National-Scale Disbursement Platforms with Real-Time, Multi-Rail Payments
all.venue: International Journal of Computer Trends and Technology
all.abstract: For a long time, large-scale disbursement of funds relied on overnight processing and checks. However, the emergence of instant payment systems like the FedNow Service from the Federal Reserve and the RTP network from The Clearing House, as well as push-to-card and digital wallet payment systems, allows for the funds to be delivered to the recipients in seconds [2][3]. Furthermore, recipients of these funds have demonstrated a strong preference for instant delivery when it is an available option [7]. However, the platforms that carry national disbursement volume were built for batch processing and cannot be taken out of service for rebuilding. This paper is a conceptual study. The aim of this study is to propose a reference architecture and a process model to enable the migration of a national-scale disbursement platform from 24-hour batch processing to near-instant multi-rail payouts while ensuring the operations of the existing platform are not interrupted. The proposed architecture introduces a layer for disbursement orchestration and rail routing that selects the fastest, least-cost eligible rail for each payout while ensuring that any fraud, anti-money-laundering, and sanctions controls are performed on each payout before it is sent. If a payment fails, the system automatically routes the payment through an alternative rail after confirming the failure of the original payment to avoid duplicate payments. A phased, reversible migration is proposed for the existing platform to the event-driven system. The proposed architecture and migration plan are evaluated using a comparison with existing literature and a scenario-based walkthrough against the proposed requirements for the platform. As this is a conceptual study, no experiments were conducted to evaluate the proposed architecture, migration plan, and requirements. The benefits of the proposed platform have been reported alongside a classification of the evidence supporting these benefits as either published data, practitioner observations, or assumptions and estimates, with empirical measurement left for future work.

all.title: Client-side brute force attack detection leveraging large language models
all.abstract: For email authentication systems, the last mile of authentication poses a critical security challenge, as attackers leverage known, real logins to bypass established server-side protections against brute-force attacks and credential stuffing. Traditional methods like rate limiting and threshold anomaly detection are ineffective against distributed, stealthy attacks that mimic normal user activity. This paper proposes a novel framework for detecting authentication sequences on the client side by leveraging lightweight Large Language Models (LLMs) in real time. Unlike signature-based approaches, the proposed framework can "explain" the temporal and contextual characteristics of login behavior and detect anomalous sequences, such as high-frequency bursts and low-and-slow last-mile reassembly attacks, without the need for predefined signatures or centralized log aggregation. The framework was tested with 2.5 million authentication sessions, 1 million of which were marked as attacks, and achieved 98.4% attack-detection accuracy with a false-positive rate of 1.2%. With an average response time of 180 ms, it achieves near real-time inference without impacting the user experience. The system was live-deployed for six months and succeeded in blocking more than 1.2 million malicious logon attempts and safeguarding more than 850,000 user accounts against traditional baselines in both scale and precision. The results demonstrate the promise of lightweight, client-side LLMs as a privacy-safe, low-resource, and robust solution for last-mile email authentication security against current and future brute force attack vectors.

all.title: CYBER CRIMES AND LEGAL REMEDIES
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The rapid growth of digital technology has increased the risk of Cyber Crimes, making effective legal remedies essential in India. This article examines the major forms of Cyber Crimes, including hacking, identity theft, online financial fraud, cyberstalking, data breaches and phishing. It analyses the legal framework addressing these offences, particularly the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The study also highlights the importance of electronic evidence, data protection, cybersecurity and constitutional rights, including privacy and freedom of speech. It discusses the remedies available to victims, such as reporting offences, initiating criminal proceedings, seeking compensation and requesting the removal of unlawful online content. Furthermore, it identifies challenges in cybercrime investigation, jurisdiction, enforcement and emerging technologies. The article concludes that effective cybercrime prevention requires stronger law enforcement, digital literacy, technological expertise, institutional cooperation and continuous legal reforms to ensure a secure and rights-respecting digital environment.

all.title: Risk-constrained human-in-the-loop repair of anti-money laundering policies: Temporal legal graphs, minimal revision, and finite-sample assurance
institutions: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology
all.abstract: This paper addresses human-in-the-loop compliance automation for obliged entities when the anti-money laundering legal corpus is amended. We treat the updating of an entity's policy as a minimal repair problem over two graphs, a versioned legal graph and a clause-and-control policy graph. The semantic difference between legal versions yields an impact cone of affected obligations, and we search for a minimally disruptive set of policy edits that satisfies them. An agentic workflow drafts, criticizes, and verifies these edits, while a learned orchestration policy decides how much machine computation and which human expert to use on each, subject to a chosen ceiling on the probability of missing a material obligation. We show that under explicit delta completeness and locality properties of the encoding, the impact cone contains every conservatively applicable obligation whose encoded legal evaluation can change across the amendment. We separately quantify the failure probability when dependency edges are missing. Moreover, minimal repair is NP-hard, and its pure coverage restriction has a logarithmic inapproximability threshold unless P=NP. A greedy method attains a logarithmic guarantee for integer-valued submodular coverage with positive additive costs. Conflicts and unresolved feasibility require separate handling and possible escalation. Finally, we show that machine acceptance can be calibrated in a distribution-free, finite-sample way, and the component guarantees compose into a single end-to-end bound on the probability of a material miss.

all.title: Compliant and Blind: Fei Qian, Trade-Based Settlement, and the Conceptual Gap in Bulgaria's Anti-Money Laundering Regime
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Bulgaria functions as a registration and logistics hub for Chinese goods entering the EU. In 2026 it completed the FATF action plan, was removed from the grey list, and achieved Compliant or Largely Compliant ratings on all forty FATF Recommendations — including a Compliant rating on Recommendation 14 (Money or Value Transfer Services). This paper argues that technical compliance has not closed the country's most consequential gap. Bulgarian enforcement and strategic frameworks continue to subsume Chinese informal value transfer systems (Fei Qian / dixia qianzhuang) under generic categories such as "Hawala," "VAT fraud," or "customs fraud." Drawing on EPPO, OLAF, FIU-SANS, MONEYVAL, FATF and Bulgarian prosecution disclosures between 2024 and 2026, and on Bulgarian and international peer-reviewed literature, the paper locates the resulting blind spot in three structural specificities: the role of Bulgarian-registered EOODs in Customs Procedure 42 fraud, the "Chinese cargo" model of customs undervaluation, and the use of straw men. It shows that the gap is not an absence of scholarship but a misalignment of categories: Bulgarian doctrine has named informal value transfer and attached it to the wrong region, the wrong trust basis, and the wrong detection indicators; the international trade-based money laundering literature has meanwhile excluded informal value transfer from its own scope. Fei Qian settlement, which is both trade-based and an IVTS, falls between the two bodies of work. The paper concludes with implications for detection and a call for a dedicated Fei Qian threat category in Bulgaria's national risk assessment, calibrated to the digital rails on which settlement now runs.

all.title: AI-Driven Financial Fraud Auditing and Evidence Chain Construction in Smart Manufacturing
all.venue: ICST Transactions on Scalable Information Systems
all.abstract: INTRODUCTION: In smart manufacturing enterprises, procurement, production, warehousing, sales, and financial settlement data are distributed across multiple business systems. Financial fraud increasingly involves cross-entity collusion, nested business chains, and fragmented evidence, making it difficult for traditional sampling audits to simultaneously ensure accurate risk identification, efficient verification, and traceable evidence support. OBJECTIVES: To address fragmented cross-system associations among manufacturing audit data, difficulties in tracing multi-hop fraud propagation across business entities, and insufficient evidence support for model-generated risk alerts, this study develops an AI-driven financial fraud auditing framework tailored to smart manufacturing processes. The framework links fraud risk identification, dynamic audit-path optimization, and verifiable evidence-chain construction within a unified closed-loop procedure. METHODS: Multi-source heterogeneous audit samples are constructed through entity matching, temporal alignment, and data-quality filtering. Business process constraints are introduced to encode inconsistencies in transaction amounts, material quantities, event timing, and entity relationships. A heterogeneous graph neural network jointly identifies high-risk entities, anomalous transactions, and fraud categories while tracing cross-entity risk propagation paths. The audit process is further formulated as a sequential decision-making task, in which deep reinforcement learning dynamically selects verification actions according to risk information gain, execution cost, and evidence sufficiency. Original records, risk relationships, audit actions, and review statuses are subsequently organized into a structured and traceable evidence chain. RESULTS:Simulation experiments show that the proposed method achieves an F1 score of 92.7% and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 98.4% for fraud detection, together with a 90.7% recall rate for risk propagation paths. Evidence completeness reaches 95.4%, while the average number of audit steps required to establish a complete evidence chain decreases to 6.9. Direct real-world testing was further conducted on three anonymized manufacturing enterprises containing 715,220 raw cross-system records and 3,660 independently audited business chains. With all trained parameters and decision thresholds fixed, the framework identified 271 of 307 confirmed anomalous chains and achieved a pooled Precision of 89.74%, Recall of 88.27%, F1 score of 89.00%, AUC of 0.956, and false alarm rate of 0.92%. Risk-propagation-path recall and evidence completeness reached 86.64% and 92.18%, respectively, while the average number of audit steps was 7.5. CONCLUSION: Integrating business-process-constrained heterogeneous graph reasoning, risk-feedback-driven audit decision-making, and structured evidence verification enables complex financial fraud to be identified, localized, and substantiated within a unified audit workflow. The proposed framework extends conventional fraud detection from isolated risk classification toward traceable cross-entity reasoning and evidence-supported audit decision-making in smart manufacturing environments.

all.title: TSL-GFDN: temporally-aware soft structural learning for group-based fraud detection network
all.abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy has fostered a complex fraud ecosystem in which group-based attacks, including Sockpuppet-based Targeted Attacks on Reviewing Systems (STARS), manifest as both dense interaction structures and coordinated temporal bursts. Graph neural networks for cohesive subgraph mining have advanced fraud detection, but existing methods often rely on static, discrete core decompositions, such as k- core and ( α , β )-core analyses. These hard structural operations are limited by an inability to model temporal coordination, which ignores the temporal synchronization of fraudulent behavior, and by loss of information near hard thresholds, which limits the model’s use of near-boundary structural signals. We propose T emporally Aware S oft Structural L earning for G roup-based F raud D etection N etwork (TSL-GFDN), a temporally aware extension of GFDN that integrates sliding-window temporal weighting into soft ( α , β )-core feature learning. TSL-GFDN maps temporally weighted degree margins to continuous soft membership scores and uses a temporal risk intensity autoencoder to support community discovery, edge classification, and vertex classification. On the real-world TianChi e-commerce dataset, where fraud exhibits clear spatiotemporal concentration, TSL-GFDN improves F1-score by 13.1% and precision by 25.4% relative to GFDN. On Bitcoin Alpha and Bitcoin OTC, the advantage is more limited because the hub-dominated topology and synthetic attack labels provide little within-density temporal variation. These results show both the value and the boundary of temporal structural learning for group-based fraud detection.

all.title: Deepfake Image Detection Using Transfer Learning Techniques
all.venue: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering Management & Applied Science
all.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning and generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic artificial images and videos, commonly known as deepfakes. These manipulated media pose significant challenges to digital security, identity verification, privacy, and information authenticity. Consequently, developing reliable techniques for detecting deepfake content has become an important research challenge. This study proposes a deep learning-based approach for detecting manipulated facial images using transfer learning with the MobileNetV2 architecture. The experimental dataset consists of 1,081 real facial images and 960 fake facial images, with the latter obtained through frame extraction from videos available in the FaceForensics++ dataset. The pre-trained MobileNetV2 model is adapted for binary classification by incorporating global average pooling, a fully connected dense layer, dropout regularization, and a sigmoid output layer. The model is trained to classify facial images into two categories: real and fake. Its performance is evaluated using standard classification metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, and Precision-Recall curve. The experimental findings demonstrate the potential of transfer learning for identifying manipulated facial images using a lightweight convolutional neural network architecture. The study highlights the applicability of MobileNetV2 for deepfake image classification under limited-data conditions and identifies dataset diversity and generalization across different sources as important considerations for further research.

all.title: Resource-Efficient Deepfake Detection with Cross Dataset Evaluation and Web Deployment
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
institutions: MIT Art, Design and Technology University
all.abstract: Generative adversarial networks and diffusion-based synthesis have made photo-realistic facial manipulation — commonly called deepfakes - inexpensive, fast and widely accessible. Such synthetic media is increasingly used for misinformation, impersonation, financial fraud and reputational attack, and human observers perform poorly at distinguishing it from authentic content. Detection methods reported in the literature achieve high accuracy when training and test manipulations originate from the same generator, but degrade sharply on unseen generation techniques, and most are released as research code rather than as usable end-to-end systems. This paper presents DeepGuard, an applied detection framework that couples MTCNN-based face detection and alignment, interval-based frame sampling for video input, and an ImageNet-pretrained XceptionNet backbone fine-tuned by two-stage transfer learning, into a single pipeline that classifies an uploaded image or video as real or deepfake and returns a confidence score. The contribution is not a new network topology but an engineered, reproducible pipeline together with a controlled comparison of convolutional backbones under one fixed preprocessing and video-disjoint splitting protocol. The system was evaluated on the Face Forensics++ (c23) corpus using a 70/15/15 split partitioned by source video, and achieved 92.40% accuracy, 93.10% precision, 91.80% recall, an F1-score of 0.9244 and a ROC-AUC of 0.9612 on the held-out test set. Limitations concerning cross-generator generalisation, compression robustness and audio-driven forgeries are analysed, and directions for extending the framework are outlined.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence and Electoral Governance: Regulatory Challenges, Political Disinformation, and the Future of Electoral Integrity
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the most important and disruptive innovations that influence modern election governance. AI technologies help with voter registration, improving the allocation of resources for elections, fraud detection, outreach to voters and other administrative processes. However, these same technologies also pose serious threats to the integrity, fairness and transparency of elections. Artificial intelligence has brought about political misinformation, creation of synthetic media (deepfakes), algorithmic microtargeting, and automated bot networks. These changes have altered the information environment where elections take place and created conditions for manipulation, suppression, and trust erosion. This paper conducts a doctrinal and comparative analytical framework to examine AI and electoral governance interaction. Using the primary legal sources- the legislation, the judicial decisions, and the official regulatory advisories- along with the secondary scholarship, it examines the adequacy of the existing frameworks in India and selected international jurisdictions which include the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, South Korea and Brazil. The study analyses India’s regulatory response comprising the advisories of the Election Commission of India in May 2024, January 2025 and October 2025; the Information Technology Act 2000 and the Intermediary Rules made under it (including the 2026 amendment on synthetically generated information); the Representation of the People Act 1951; and the Model Code of Conduct identifies continuing legal and institutional gaps, and makes recommendations for a rights-preserving, technology-agnostic regulatory architecture. Any factual and legal proposition that appears in the text is footnoted and unless otherwise stated was checked against the cited source as on 15 October 2026.

all.title: KIBERFIRIBGARLAR TOMONIDAN QO'LLANILADIGAN IJTIMOIY MUHANDISLIK TAKTIKALARINI TAHLIL QILISHNING O'ZIGA XOS XUSUSIYATLARI
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Maqolada axborot-kommunikatsiya texnologiyalari jadal rivojlanayotgan sharoitda kiberfiribgarlar tomonidan qo'llaniladigan ijtimoiy muhandislik (social engineering) taktikalarining kriminologik, kriminalistik va psixologik xususiyatlari tadqiq etilgan. O'zbekiston Respublikasining Jinoyat kodeksi (168-modda), «Kiberxavfsizlik to'g'risida»gi va «Shaxsga doir ma'lumotlar to'g'risida»gi qonunlari normalari asosida fishing, vishing, smishing, soxta bank-moliya va davlat organlari niqobi ostidagi manipulyatsiya usullarini tahlil qilish mexanizmlari ko'rib chiqilgan. Kiberjinoyatlarni aniqlash va tahlil qilish amaliyotidagi muammolar ko'rsatilib, ijtimoiy muhandislik hujumlariga qarshi kurashish va ularni tahlil qilish tizimini takomillashtirish yuzasidan ilmiy-amaliy takliflar ishlab chiqilgan.

all.title: Victimized and Unprepared: Financial Fraud Experience and Retirement Saving
institutions: Chongqing University of Arts and Sciences
all.abstract: As population aging and pension reform place greater responsibility for retirement security on individuals, understanding the barriers to adequate retirement saving has become increasingly important. Using nationally representative microdata from the China Aging Finance Survey for 2020–2023, we examine the relationship between financial fraud experience and two dimensions of retirement saving: participation and accumulated reserves. The results show that individuals with fraud experience are significantly less likely to participate in retirement saving and hold lower retirement reserves. Mechanism analyses provide evidence consistent with three pathways: reduced risk tolerance, greater financial exclusion, and distorted retirement-planning cognition. These adverse associations are particularly pronounced among rural residents, low-income households, individuals without basic pension coverage, and older respondents. The study extends the literature on life-cycle saving by highlighting how adverse financial experiences are associated with subsequent long-term financial engagement and retirement preparation. The findings underscore the importance of fraud prevention and consumer protection and, more broadly, suggest potential roles for accessible redress, targeted financial education, and broader pension protection in strengthening retirement resilience among financially vulnerable households.

all.title: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
institutions: The University of Texas at Arlington
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
all.abstract: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. To investigate family intervention barriers to elder scams, we collected 2M Reddit posts from May 2021 to June 2026 and 2B Baidu Tieba posts from 2007 to 2026. The final corpora contain 13,082 Reddit posts and 3,933 Baidu Tieba posts, labeled using platform-specific codebooks, manual reference annotations, and LLM coding. Through a mixed-methods analysis, we find that scams often extend beyond a single incident and are reported alongside debt problems and broken family relationships. In 68.0\% of Reddit posts recording reactions, older adults showed resistance or continued involvement; in Baidu Tieba family-confrontation posts, 41.9\% showed continued belief. Relatives identified fraud in 74.4\% of Reddit posts and narrated cases on Baidu Tieba, but without the victim's consent, relatives may lack the legal authority to intervene. In Reddit posts recording reactions, account locks or credential changes appeared in 8.9\% under resistance or continued involvement, compared with 33.3\% under acceptance. Measures such as phone or network monitoring and financial takeover were reported more often under resistance. Recovering funds is very limited in posts recording follow-up results of fraud; Baidu Tieba users reported that police classified older adults' voluntary transfers as civil disputes.

all.title: Policy brief: Protection of Indonesian students and citizens in Turkey: challenges and recommendations
all.abstract: Indonesian students in Turkey who convert rupiah into Turkish lira frequently rely on exchange services offered by fellow members of the diaspora. This arrangement fills a real gap left by formal banking, yet it also exposes students to fraud, and victims seldom seek legal remedy because they distrust institutions and know little about Turkish law. Drawing on the author’s four years of study in Turkey and on peer-reviewed research about international students, informal value transfer, migrants’ trust in law enforcement, and legal literacy, this policy brief examines why fraud in informal currency exchange persists and how Indonesian and Turkish authorities can respond. It compares four courses of action and recommends a combined package: a criteria-based verification service with a secure transaction platform, legal-literacy and reporting support developed with student associations, and a coordination channel with Turkish authorities, with an official low-cost exchange channel as a medium-term goal. The brief also assesses the main risks, including the legal feasibility of the proposed rehabilitation period, and identifies where evidence from Turkey is still missing.

all.title: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence in Forensic Accounting: Detecting Fraud, Anomalies, and Financial Risks
all.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly applied in forensic accounting to detect fraud, anomalies, and financial risks across large transaction populations. This chapter reviews AI applications in forensic accounting, fraud detection, auditing, and sustainable reporting, with emphasis on detection performance, data requirements, interpretability, and forensic usability. It examines key AI and ML techniques and discusses practical challenges including class imbalance, false positives and negatives, overfitting, data leakage, concept drift, and model validation. The chapter also considers AI-supported verification of (ESG) and (CSR) disclosures and the supporting roles of blockchain and big data analytics. Drawing on the reviewed evidence, it proposes a conceptual framework in which AI-enabled detection contributes to reliable financial and sustainability reporting when supported by data quality, regulatory maturity, auditor expertise, and explainability. The chapter concludes that AI should augment, rather than replace, professional forensic judgment

all.title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?
all.abstract: Online fraud is traditionally limited by the cost of the human labor needed to talk to potential victims. We ask whether hosted large language models will now supply that labor. We prompted ten off-the-shelf models to play the seller in the "free item, just pay delivery" advance-fee scam common on buy-and-sell sites, using a plain system prompt with no jailbreak. Each model played 30 conversations against each of four buyer personas, from credulous to guarded, with the same model playing the buyer (1,200 conversations). We label each conversation by what happened to the buyer's money, and validate the labels against two human coders. 737 conversations (61%) ended with the buyer paying in advance. Eight of the ten models played in almost every conversation, and running both sides cost about 2.5 cents per payment. Only the guarded buyer, who wanted a findable identity, resisted, and the most willing sellers got past it by inventing names and phone numbers. Sellers that recognized the scam still took the money in 133 conversations, usually reasoning about their own honesty rather than the buyer's risk. Several models protected the buyer without refusing, by conceding payment on delivery, so refusal rates alone misstate safety. We release the benchmark, prompts, code and labels.

all.title: JevRisk: Zero-Shot Financial Risk Assessment with a Language Decision Model
all.abstract: Banks must monitor every customer's financial risk, such as money laundering and credit default, by interpreting financial activity in the context of the customer's profile. Existing risk monitoring systems of banks are mostly based on expert-designed risk indicators, which apply predefined thresholds to every customer and cannot adapt to their personal situations. Supervised models recognise risk patterns from labelled customers, but each label often needs an expert's review or months of repayment history, which is slow and costly. Financial risk assessment therefore calls for a zero-shot decision system that minimises the need for labels and generalises across customers and risk types. To this end, we present JevRisk, a system for zero-shot financial risk assessment with a language decision model. JevRisk works in two steps. First, following regulatory guidelines in the finance domain, JevRisk computes exact risk indicators with code. Second, the language decision model (e.g., \jev{}) reads these indicators together with the customer's profile and activity, judges the case in context with broad world knowledge, and returns the score of high risk. We evaluate JevRisk on the anti-money laundering task with public synthetic data from Scotiabank and on the credit risk task with real data from Home Credit and Lending Club. On both tasks, JevRisk outperforms rule-based and unsupervised methods, and is on par with or better than supervised methods (e.g., GBDT and TabPFN) trained on about a thousand labelled customers.

all.title: Proving a negative is difficult: positive and unlabeled financial statement fraud detection via multi-modal graph auto-encoders
RAFT-Phish: Robust phishing detection under retrieval contamination
Levelling the playing field: A social identity-based three-stage DEA model for efficiency evaluation free from psychological bias
Efficient HMM-Based Interpretable Customer Representation for Customer Segmentation in Banking
all.abstract: Customer segmentation is a fundamental component of banking decision-support systems, supporting applications such as targeted marketing, risk management, fraud detection, and strategic planning. Existing approaches generally combine feature extraction with clustering, relying on either static or dynamic \textit{Recency--Frequency--Monetary} (RFM) representations or deep learning models. However, RFM-based methods often fail to capture the sequential dynamics of customer behavior, while deep learning approaches typically produce latent representations that are difficult to interpret and frequently require additional dimensionality reduction for visualization. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the \textit{Sequential Amounts and Sequential Intensity} (SASI) framework, an interpretable customer representation method based on Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). Unlike conventional deterministic approaches, HMMs provide a probabilistic framework for modeling sequential variations in transaction amounts and transactional intensity. The meta-data extracted from the learned HMMs are transformed into a two-dimensional embedding, whose axes directly reflect these two behavioral dimensions. Experiments conducted on $1{,}503$ and $2{,}039$ customers from the synthetic \textit{Nigerian Retail Banking Transactions (Nigerian)} and the real-world \textit{PKDD'99 (Berka)} datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SASI using the \textit{Silhouette Coefficient} (SC), \textit{Davies--Bouldin Index} (DBI), and \textit{Calinski--Harabasz Index} (CHI). When SASI is compared with the competing methods, it achieves the second-best $\mathrm{SC}$ ($0.650635$), the best $\mathrm{DBI}$ ($0.418718$), and the best $\mathrm{CHI}$ ($6578.11$) on the \textit{Nigerian} dataset. On the \textit{Berka} dataset, it attains the best $\mathrm{SC}$ ($0.507139$), the best $\mathrm{DBI}$ ($0.500209$), and the second-best $\mathrm{CHI}$ ($3309.01$). These results establish SASI as an effective operational framework, combining competitive clustering performance with fully interpretable and directly visualizable customer representations.

all.title: Quantum Computing for Financial Analytics and Risk Management
all.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
all.abstract: This chapter explores the integration of quantum computing into financial analytics, focusing on applications in financial markets, risk management, and accounting. It examines how quantum principles and algorithms, including QAOA, VQE, and HHL, can support portfolio optimization, derivatives pricing, credit risk modeling, and fraud detection. The chapter also considers quantum machine learning for analysing ESG metrics, sentiment data, and unstructured corporate information. Case studies from banking, FinTech, and national quantum initiatives illustrate emerging adoption, while ethical, regulatory, and infrastructure challenges are discussed alongside hybrid quantum-classical approaches. The chapter concludes with a research agenda for quantum finance, corporate governance, and accounting.

all.title: Enhancing Forensic Accounting with Data Analytics: An Empirical Study of Financial Risk Mitigation and Insolvency Prediction
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: In an increasingly complex and digitalized financial environment, the detection and prevention of corporate fraud and financial distress have become critical for investors, lenders, regulators, and corporate governance bodies. This study examines the integration of data analytics and forensic accounting to enhance fraud detection and insolvency prediction. Using a comprehensive case study of Bhushan Steel Limited (BSL), the research evaluates the effectiveness of the Altman Z-Score and Beneish M-Score models over a fifteen-year period (2012–13 to 2025–26). The findings indicate that the Altman Z-Score consistently identified financial distress and insolvency risk well before the company’s collapse, demonstrating strong predictive capability. In contrast, the Beneish M-Score detected earnings manipulation only during specific periods, reflecting limitations in identifying long-term structural deterioration. Statistical analysis further confirms the significance of both models in assessing financial reporting risks, although the Beneish framework exhibited greater variability. The study highlights the value of integrating traditional forensic accounting techniques with advanced data analytics and AI-driven systems to improve early warning mechanisms, strengthen corporate transparency, support informed decision-making, and enhance financial stability. The findings provide practical insights for regulators, financial institutions, auditors, and investors seeking proactive approaches to risk management and fraud prevention.

all.title: The Mediating Role of Digital Literacy Between Financial Literacy and Investment Scam Awareness
all.venue: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance
all.abstract: This study analyses whether digital literacy mediates the relationship between financial literacy and investment scam awareness. Despite the rapid expansion of digital financial services, there remains limited knowledge of whether financial and digital literacy interact to shape resistance to online investment scams. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among undergraduates who were selected through stratified random sampling in Sri Lanka. Financial literacy is measured through budgeting skills, financial attitude, financial product literacy and risk awareness. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to estimate the direct effects and mediating effects. Budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness enhance digital literacy, while financial attitude shows no meaningful effect. Digital literacy exhibits the strongest direct influence on investment scam awareness. Mediation analysis confirms that digital literacy transmits the effects of budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness to scam awareness, whereas financial attitude remains non-significant. The study conceptualizes digital literacy as a coping appraisal mechanism that enables individuals to operationalize financial knowledge in digital financial environments. Guided by Protection Motivation Theory, the study interprets financial literacy as supporting threat appraisal and digital literacy as supporting coping appraisal. The single institution, cross-sectional and self-reported design may restrict generalizability and causal inference. Future studies should use multi-site samples, longitudinal designs, fraud simulation experiments.

all.title: A TUTELA COLETIVA DOS IDOSOS FRENTE ÀS FRAUDES TECNOLÓGICAS: A ATUAÇÃO DA DEFENSORIA PÚBLICA DO AMAZONAS À LUZ DA LGPD EM MANAUS
all.venue: Journal of Law and Sustainable Development
all.abstract: Este artigo analisa a atuação da Defensoria Pública do Estado do Amazonas na tutela coletiva de pessoas idosas vítimas de fraudes tecnológicas, com especial atenção aos impactos da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD) no município de Manaus. A pesquisa parte da percepção de que a digitalização dos serviços bancários e das relações de consumo trouxe facilidades importantes, mas também criou novos espaços de exposição para pessoas que nem sempre tiveram oportunidade de desenvolver familiaridade com ferramentas digitais. No caso da população idosa, fatores técnicos, informacionais, econômicos e sociais podem se somar, produzindo uma situação de hipervulnerabilidade. Entre as práticas identificadas no material que fundamenta o estudo estão a clonagem de dados, as fraudes bancárias, os empréstimos consignados não autorizados, os golpes do falso funcionário, o phishing e as transferências fraudulentas realizadas por PIX. O problema ultrapassa a dimensão patrimonial, pois uma fraude pode atingir a dignidade, a autonomia, a tranquilidade e a confiança da vítima. Nesse cenário, a Defensoria Pública exerce papel relevante por sua possibilidade de atuação judicial e extrajudicial, individual e coletiva. O estudo articula Constituição Federal, Estatuto da Pessoa Idosa, Código de Defesa do Consumidor e LGPD, buscando compreender como esses instrumentos podem funcionar de maneira integrada. A metodologia é bibliográfica e qualitativa, considerando fontes em língua portuguesa publicadas entre 2021 e 2026, especialmente nas bases SciELO e Google Acadêmico. A análise reforça a importância de uma proteção jurídica diferenciada, preventiva e humanizada, capaz de enfrentar não apenas o dano já ocorrido, mas também as estruturas e práticas que favorecem a repetição das fraudes.

all.title: Conecta 60+: Inclusão Digital e Segurança na Internet para Pessoas Idosas: Relato de Experiência
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Este trabalho apresenta o projeto Conecta 60+, iniciativa acadêmica de inclusão digital e promoção da segurança na internet para pessoas idosas. A proposta foi motivada pelas dificuldades de utilização de smartphones, redes sociais e serviços financeiros digitais, bem como pelos riscos de fraudes e exposição de dados pessoais. O objetivo foi favorecer a autonomia digital por meio de orientações acessíveis e atividades práticas. O planejamento contemplou 12 encontros presenciais, com carga horária total de 24 horas e turmas de até 10 participantes. Os conteúdos incluíram comunicação por aplicativos, uso de redes sociais, proteção de senhas, identificação de mensagens fraudulentas e cuidados com o Pix. A metodologia envolveu demonstrações, exercícios assistidos, simulações de situações de risco e acompanhamento da aprendizagem. A experiência relatada contou com cinco participantes e permitiu observar maior confiança na utilização de recursos digitais, redução da insegurança diante da tecnologia e ampliação das possibilidades de interação no ambiente virtual. Os resultados, de natureza qualitativa, indicam a relevância de ações educativas adaptadas ao ritmo de aprendizagem desse público.

institutions: Larbi Ben M'hidi University of Oum El Bouaghi
all.abstract: The accelerated use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing the financial services industry and the banking sector in terms of improving the efficiency of their operations, customer experience, risk management and the effectiveness of strategic decision-making. The proposed researc examines the profound influence of artificial intelligence (AI) on the financial sector, analyzing its many effects on operations, risk management and client experiences. By examining the incorporation of machine learning algorithms, natural language processing and robotic process automation, the substantial improvements in efficiency and reductions in costs that Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides to financial institutions was revealed. Moreover, the study explores the consequences of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in improving fraud detection procedures and reducing operational risks, thereby strengthening the sector's ability to withstand challenges. Nevertheless, the study also acknowledges the risks related to data privacy, ethical considerations and the possibility of employment displacement, emphasizing the necessity for strong regulatory frameworks.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Privacy Paradox for Secure AI Operations
all.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into critical domains, including healthcare, finance, and public surveillance, has illuminated a fundamental tension between data-driven innovation and individual privacy protection. This chapter comprehensively investigates the AI-privacy paradox through rigorous empirical validation using real-world datasets from diverse domains: the Diabetes Health Indicators Dataset (healthcare), Credit Card Fraud Detection Dataset (financial), and UCI Adult Census Dataset (demographic) for intelligent system optimization and protecting personal privacy rights. Our experimental results show that privacy-preserving AI techniques achieve practical viability. Differential privacy mechanisms with ϵ-values of 0.5-1.0 maintain 86.7-90.0% model accuracy while providing substantial privacy guarantees across all domains. Federated learning architectures preserve 97.7-98.2% of centralized performance while eliminating raw data exposure, with communication overhead of https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> 1.8 − 2.2 × . Privacy attack implementation shows significant improvements, reducing membership inference attack success rates from 74.2% to 49.9% on demographic data and increasing model inversion reconstruction errors from 0.893 to 1.427 on healthcare data. The multi-dimensional risk assessment reveals domain-specific patterns, with healthcare applications exhibiting the highest risk profile (1.667) compared to financial (0.575) and demographic (0.151) applications. Hybrid approaches combining multiple privacy techniques achieve 56.4% overall risk reduction while maintaining functional utility. This work establishes that the AI-privacy paradox can be effectively resolved through context-aware implementation of privacy-preserving technologies, providing a validated framework for secure AI operations across sensitive domains.

all.title: Credential Stuffing Report
A Multi-Dimension EML Feature Framework and Multi-Model-Based Email Anomaly Detection System
institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
all.abstract: Detecting business email compromise (BEC), account takeover (ATO), and insider threats that use legitimate accounts and business language requires analyzing the sender’s role and prior conversations alongside a message’s technical attributes. However, because data combining corporate email with human resources information is subject to restrictions regarding access to personal and proprietary business information, it is difficult to study organizational roles and communication relationships simultaneously. We propose a multi-dimensional UBA feature framework that integrates raw EML files, MTA logs, and role and authority information from ERP, together with a synthetic email corpus of a fictional company, NexaSoft. Based on an organization of 126 employees and 117 normal business scenarios, we define 23 feature-based and 11 contextual anomaly types and build a dataset of 124,355 emails (76,850 normal, 47,505 anomalous), organized into feature-based and context-based datasets. Linking each message to organizational roles and reply relationships allows normal work and anomalous requests to be represented in the same organizational and conversational environment. The detection method comprises a rule layer for explicit security conditions, an XGBoost layer for structural and statistical anomalies, and a multi-view layer for context-dependent anomalies, in which models M1–M4 analyze message semantics, behavior and time, organizational role and policy, and past conversation. On their assigned classes, M1, M2, and M3 achieve Macro-F1 of 0.9863, 0.9752, and 0.9110 under scenario-separated evaluation, and M4 achieves a mean Macro-F1 of 0.9213 over three seeds. Removing prior conversation lowers M4’s Macro-F1 by 4.34 pp, confirming its contribution. The dataset and detection framework thus enable the study and evaluation of both technical and context-dependent email anomalies, grounded in organizational roles and conversation flow, in one business environment.

all.title: Research Note—Teaching Financial Social Work in Social Work Education: A Brief Update
all.abstract: Despite the growing financial vulnerability of many U.S. households, schools of social work have been slow to take up curricular changes that adequately prepare practitioners for financial social work (FSW). This research note reports on a survey using a convenience sample of 54 U.S. social work faculty who have expressed interest in FSW. Results suggest that while some topics are commonly taught (e.g., financial practice with communities, household income, and credit and debt), other important topics are rarely covered (e.g., financial fraud, identity theft, collections, garnishment, bankruptcy, and insurance). Of the FSW content currently taught, most is included in existing courses. However, there are some courses entirely devoted to FSW. The results further suggest that dissemination of practical course materials may encourage faculty to teach new FSW topics. Researchers and practitioners should increase both the visibility and incentives for teaching financial topics in social work education.

all.title: AI-Based Fake Document Verification System
all.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Aniket Ramchandra Patil Tushar Manohar Patil
Bhagya Basappa Pattanshetti Pranav Bharat Sanabe
all.abstract: The rapid shift from paper-based administration to digital documentation has accelerated information sharing, but it has also made document forgery more likely. Altered certificates, identity proofs, academic records, invoices and other official documents, when accepted as authentic, can lead to financial loss, identity theft and administrative errors. Manual verification is slow, depends on the experience of the examiner and is difficult to scale. This paper presents the design of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Fake Document Verification System that integrates machine learning, optical character recognition (OCR), image processing and rule-based validation to help identify suspicious documents. The main objectives are to extract information from documents, detect visual and structural irregularities, compare the extracted details with expected formats or trusted records, and produce a risk assessment that a human reviewer can understand. The scope covers uploaded PDF documents and scanned images that may be used in public service workflows, banking, insurance, hiring and educational institutions. Following a review of published research and technical standards, the paper proposes a seven-stage framework comprising document upload, preprocessing, text extraction, visual-forensic analysis, structural and semantic validation, trusted-source verification, and risk assessment with report generation. The advantages and limitations of automated verification are also discussed, including image quality, unseen forgery techniques, privacy, bias and incorrect decisions..

all.title: BOUNDARY OMEGA v100 — Zero Silent Null Void: Universal Recoverability-Constrained Systems, META SELF Generation, Fair Judgment, Operational Law, Continuity Science, and Recursive Governance
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: BOUNDARY is a cumulative, interdisciplinary research and systems-engineering corpus integrating Recoverability-Constrained Systems (RCS), Continuity Science, finite successor-space reasoning, recoverability-constrained admissibility, recursive governance, distinction boundaries, evidence preservation, institutional accountability, living-system protection, and cross-domain operational architectures. This publication consolidates the historical BOUNDARY development sequence through version 90 into a single integrated archive. The corpus contains foundational research materials, proposed mathematical and conceptual structures, operational protocols, model governance and legal instruments, cybersecurity and identity-protection architectures, ethical safeguards, technical specifications, scenario-generation methods, executable Python prototypes, automated tests, and successive adversarial-review editions. The central research question is how individuals, institutions, technologies, and interconnected systems can make consequential decisions while preserving safety, rights, evidence, accountability, correction mechanisms, and recoverable future options. Foundational Architecture The corpus develops a common framework across physical, biological, computational, financial, legal, institutional, social, environmental, and communication systems. Its recurring foundations include: Finite successor-space mathematics and recoverability-constrained decision admissibility. Continuity of persons, records, identities, services, responsibilities, and system states. Distinction boundaries separating observed facts, assumptions, hypotheses, uncertainty, and invalid procedures. Recursive governance, independent oversight, transparent decision records, and corrective review. Protection of bodily autonomy, cognitive freedom, personal privacy, freedom of belief, consent, and non-coercion. Evidence provenance, chain of custody, preservation of missing or disputed records, and recoverable institutional processes. Interoperability among domains without eliminating their distinct safety, legal, or evidentiary requirements. The ZERO / NULL / VOID / SILENCE framework is used as a scoped distinction model: ZERO: verified absence within a defined observation or test boundary. NULL: unknown, unavailable, insufficient, or unresolved information. VOID: a process or decision identified as invalid under specified criteria, subject to applicable law and review. SILENCE: nonresponse, absence of communication, or an intentionally protected boundary; its significance depends on consent, duty, context, and evidence. These categories are not interchangeable and do not independently establish wrongdoing, consciousness, identity, safety, or legal liability. Nine-Way Operational Continuity Protocol The integrated architecture uses nine interconnected operations: Detect — identify events, risks, claims, failures, and relevant distinctions. Preserve — secure records, evidence, rights, resources, and future options. Verify — assess provenance, authority, identity, consent, uncertainty, and independent corroboration. Protect — apply proportionate safeguards against credible harm. Communicate — provide accessible notices, explanations, responsible contacts, and response pathways. Intervene — initiate authorized, proportionate, time-sensitive corrective action. Audit — document decisions, inspect controls, test outcomes, and establish accountability. Recover — restore services, access, records, capabilities, and lawful alternatives where possible. Reassess — reopen conclusions when evidence, circumstances, risks, or applicable requirements change. The operations are recursive rather than strictly linear. A later discovery can reopen an earlier determination, and no automated assessment substitutes for qualified human judgment where required. Integrated Research and Application Domains The historical corpus addresses interconnected applications in: Artificial intelligence and computation: model reliability, AI governance, synthetic identity, deepfakes, impersonation, provenance, human-machine interfaces, predictive sufficiency, recursive model collapse, AI convergence, and responsible automation. Cybersecurity and digital continuity: account protection, identity restoration, unauthorized access, hardware and software integrity, communication resilience, deleted records, missing emails, platform failures, digital evidence, secure authentication, and incident recovery. Healthcare and living systems: patient safety, care continuity, informed consent, medical triage, clinical communication, disability inclusion, rehabilitation, healthcare governance, institutional inspection, and recovery pathways. Finance and economic systems: financial continuity, payment and access architectures, trading-performance verification, public-resource accountability, inflation-related vulnerability, financial evidence, and recoverable economic decisions. Law, public administration, and governance: model constitutional and statutory provisions, citizen complaint procedures, institutional response duties, non-disclosure safeguards, independent inspection, whistleblower protection, public accountability, and cross-border cooperation. Communication and identity: accessible communication, provenance of messages and media, protection against unauthorized identity substitution, social-media interaction integrity, archival continuity, and safeguards for private communications. Community and social systems: education, sports and boxing safety, youth safeguarding, community development, social assistance, humanitarian access, personal autonomy, non-discrimination, and shared responsibility. Environment and infrastructure: water systems, environmental continuity, climate-related hazards, physical-device resilience, resource access, and recovery from infrastructure disruption. Scientific and conceptual extensions: quantum-system proposals, consciousness-related research questions, biological-computational interfaces, distinction theory, recursive architectures, and theoretical extensions to hypothetical future environments and civilizations. The presence of a conceptual or speculative domain does not constitute empirical confirmation of its premises. Integrated Archive and Historical Continuity The archive preserves successive BOUNDARY editions through version 90, including their foundational principles, domain-specific architectures, model legal provisions, executable prototypes, test scenarios, and historical development records. The later editions expand protections relating to privacy, institutional silence, missing evidence, collaborative memory, sports safety, financial-performance claims, synthetic media, human-presence verification, and adversarial failure analysis. Version 90 contributes a second-pass adversarial closure assessment covering 18 domain categories, 12 failure families, nine operational directions, and nine safeguards, producing 17,496 finite structural test configurations. The included executable systems are offline decision-support and evaluation prototypes. Their automated tests establish results only for the implemented test cases, not universal security, legal validity, clinical efficacy, or operational deployment. Research Methodology The corpus combines conceptual formalization, cross-domain systems analysis, requirements engineering, threat modeling, adversarial scenario design, proposed governance controls, legal-model drafting, software prototyping, automated testing, and recursive review. Where the archive contains public statements, screenshots, hypothetical cases, or disputed allegations, those materials are treated according to their evidentiary status. They are not automatically accepted as verified descriptions of events. Scope and Limitations BOUNDARY is presented as a research and proposed implementation framework, not as an enacted global legal system, certified medical device, autonomous enforcement platform, or demonstrated universal solution. No finite scenario set can exhaust every possible future event, adversary, jurisdiction, interpretation, or technological development. Claims concerning unobserved civilizations, metaphysical entities, parallel realities, spiritual mechanisms, or the nature of consciousness remain conceptual or philosophical unless supported by independently verifiable evidence. The archive therefore preserves explicit uncertainty, reviewability, human rights, non-coercion, and the possibility of future correction. Contribution The principal contribution is an integrated approach to consequential systems in which protection, recoverability, evidence integrity, governance, and accountability are treated as interconnected design requirements rather than isolated domain-specific concerns. The corpus provides a basis for further formal analysis, independent replication, interdisciplinary criticism, software development, policy evaluation, and empirical validation. Core principle: Protect living beings and fundamental rights; preserve evidence and recoverable futures; distinguish knowledge from uncertainty; and ensure that consequential decisions remain accountable, proportionate, and open to correction.

all.title: Machine Learning Techniques in Blockchain Forensics for Crypto Crime Detection
all.abstract: The rise of cryptocurrencies has contributed to the ultra-Orth develops in the sphere of financial technology, and it has also brought forth the problems of illegal practices, including money laundering, scams, and ransomware attacks. Blockchain has brought transparency and immutability, but it also has the downside of enabling pseudonymous transactions, which can render the investigation of a crime difficult. Conventional processes of solving crypto crimes have difficulty in detecting the vast amount of blockchain data and its highly complicated nature. The chapter examines how machine learning (ML) can be used to solve these problems in the field of blockchain forensics. Cryptocurrency crimes can be detected and prevented to a great degree with the help of machine learning, which can be implemented through supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly-based techniques, and graphs. Some of the examples of various ML models that are evaluated depending on their compliance in the detection of fraudulent purchases and suspicious wallet type of fraud include decision trees, support vector machine (SVM), and graph neural networks (GNNs). It is discussed why these models can be integrated with the current forensic tools, what issues in data privacy require attention, and what future areas of research are suggested to improve detection systems. The results support the encouraging potential of applying ML techniques to enhance the precision and efficiency of crypto crime detection, although weaknesses like imbalance in the data and evasion strategies remain to be addressed. The chapter adds to the field of dynamic blockchain forensics, focusing on the opportunities presented by machine learning to stem the processes of cryptocurrency-related crimes.

all.title: Deep Learning and Graph Analytics in Crypto Wallet Clustering and Attribution Techniques for Blockchain Forensics
all.abstract: The blockchain technology is behind an expanding list of decentralized financial services, digital currencies, and peer- to-peer transactions. Although blockchain transparency (e.g., of Bitcoin and Ethereum) has the benefit of being auditable, pseudonymous addresses prevent the consideration of the actual identity of transacting parties. Crypto wallet clustering and attribution methods fill this gap by classifying addresses into groups and clusters of addresses into the real world by heuristic, machine learning, and graph-theoretic approaches. The chapter is broad in terms of the topic that it handles, the theoretical backgrounds of address clustering, advanced heuristics such as common- input-ownership (CIO), change-address detection, and CoinJoin de-mixing, and modern deep-learning and graph neural network methods. We divide and examine attribution pipelines, which combine on-chain analytics with off-chain intelligence collection and analyze real-world applications in law enforcement, anti-money-laundering (AML) compliance, exchange due diligence, and ransomware monitoring. Countermeasures that can enhance privacy and the ethical aspects of blockchain surveillance are highly considered. Precision of the cluster and accuracy of the attribution of 94.3 percent and 89.7 percent respectively have been shown in experimental results using a hybrid Graph Attention Network (GAT) model on the publicly available Elliptic dataset and Wallet Explorer- labeled graph. The chapter ends with open research questions and the future of regulatory expectations of blockchain analytics.

all.title: Tracing illicit proceeds: understanding the asset acquisition strategies of commercial sexual exploitation networks in the United States
Election Campaign Donation System
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Election Campaign Donation System: A Digital Platform for Political Fundraising, Financial Transparency, and Public Participation Description The Election Campaign Donation System (Wiper Donation System) is a proposed digital platform designed to modernize political campaign fundraising through secure donation processing, financial transparency, and improved public participation. Prepared for the Wiper Patriotic Front, the system provides a technology-driven framework through which political parties, candidates, supporters, and administrators can interact within a centralized campaign fundraising environment. The platform aims to simplify how political campaigns receive, manage, monitor, and report financial contributions while providing supporters with accessible and convenient ways to participate in campaign financing. By combining web-based services, mobile applications, integrated payment infrastructure, and real-time financial analytics, the system establishes a structured approach to managing political donations in both local and international contexts. Core Capabilities 1. Multi-Channel Donation Management The system is designed to support contributions through multiple international and regional payment providers, including M-PESA, IntaSend, Pesapal, Flutterwave, Stripe, and PayPal. It also outlines support for additional mobile money services, bank transfers, and cryptocurrency payment providers. Donors can make one-time contributions, establish recurring donations, or register future donation pledges. Multi-currency functionality is intended to accommodate contributors from different geographical regions. 2. Financial Transparency and Accountability A central component of the platform is its financial monitoring and reporting infrastructure. Candidates and authorized party administrators can access dashboards displaying fundraising progress, donation histories, transaction statuses, campaign performance, and withdrawal activities. Detailed transaction records, downloadable financial reports, and withdrawal approval workflows are designed to improve financial traceability and accountability. 3. Embedded Donation and Analytics Widgets The system introduces customizable donation and analytics widgets that can be embedded into external websites and digital campaign channels. Political candidates and authorized publishers can create branded donation interfaces, configure suggested contribution amounts, and monitor fundraising performance across different placements. Each widget is assigned a unique identifier to support donation attribution, performance monitoring, and administrative oversight. Widget approval, domain restrictions, monitoring, and suspension mechanisms are included in the proposed design. 4. Donor Engagement and Participation Supporters can explore political party profiles, review campaign information, contribute financially, and follow campaign developments through web and mobile interfaces. The platform incorporates donor privacy preferences, anonymous contribution options, digital receipts, donation histories, campaign updates, notifications, and social sharing capabilities. 5. Administrative and Compliance Management The administrative infrastructure provides tools for managing user accounts, verifying political candidates, configuring payment gateways, reviewing withdrawal requests, resolving disputes, monitoring suspicious transactions, and generating compliance reports. The proposed system also incorporates role-based access control, two-factor authentication, Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures, Anti-Money Laundering (AML) screening, transaction monitoring, and audit logs. These mechanisms are intended to support responsible financial operations and facilitate alignment with applicable electoral and financial regulations. 6. Mobile Accessibility and Internationalization The platform is designed around both a responsive web application and dedicated Android and iOS mobile applications. It considers mobile-first usage, low-bandwidth environments, multiple currencies, localization, accessibility, and offline access to cached campaign information. Technical Architecture The documented technology stack comprises: Web frontend: Next.js and Tailwind CSS. Mobile applications: Flutter for Android and iOS. Backend: Node.js with RESTful APIs. Database: PostgreSQL. Authentication: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and role-based access control. Caching and background processing: Redis, with RabbitMQ as an optional extension. Payment infrastructure: Integration with regional and international payment gateways. Communication services: Email, SMS, and mobile push notification integrations. Analytics and monitoring: Transaction reporting, operational dashboards, audit logs, and system monitoring. The architecture emphasizes modularity, secure third-party integrations, transaction reconciliation, data protection, backup and restoration strategies, and scalability. Security, Governance, and Risk Management Recognizing the financial and political sensitivity of campaign donations, the system incorporates a multi-layered security and governance framework. Its proposed safeguards include encrypted data transmission and storage, two-factor authentication, restricted administrative permissions, suspicious transaction detection, payment gateway security, audit trails, and controlled financial withdrawals. The documentation also identifies regulatory compliance, donor privacy, cross-border transactions, platform misuse, payment fraud, and system availability as important operational considerations. It references relevant frameworks and regulatory environments, including the Kenya Data Protection Act, GDPR, and PCI-DSS requirements for payment processing. Intended Application and Broader Relevance Although initially prepared for the Wiper Patriotic Front, the system's modular architecture and configurable payment infrastructure are designed with potential adaptation to different political organizations and electoral environments in mind. Its broader objective is to provide a structured digital approach to campaign financing by connecting political organizations with supporters while strengthening financial recordkeeping, transparency, accessibility, and administrative oversight. The technical documentation establishes the proposed system architecture, functional requirements, user roles, integrations, operational workflows, security considerations, and risk mitigation strategies necessary to guide implementation and future development. Document type: Technical Documentation / System Design Specification Project: Wiper Donation System Prepared for: Wiper Patriotic Front
