all.title: An attribute-augmented spectral-temporal graph-contextual transformer for fraud and anomaly detection in financial networks
all.abstract: A growing concern in consumer financial applications is the necessity of protection in the face of challenging, dynamic cyber threats. This is primarily attributed to interaction networks between users and devices becoming high dimensional and imbalanced. The classic models of securing a computer system have proven to be inadequate to describe the complex relationships of coordinated attacks, and the evolving strategies of threat actors are incompatible with static graph approaches. In this paper, authors present an attribute-augmented Graph Neural Network based framework that uses adaptive embedding dimension and multi-hop neighborhood aggregation to achieve high accuracy at the edge-level classification of malicious transactions, called Graph-Contextual Transformer (GCT). The proposed GCT model is tested on the financial transaction system data set, and the AUC is 0.756. This beats the best baseline AUC (LightGBM) by around 2% and also achieves a very impressive 26.8% relative improvement for operational Precision@5000. To increase interpretability for compliance and regulatory audits, we additionally support visualization of the nodes using t-SNE and overlays of egonets decision boundaries and identification of high risk edges. The results illustrate that embedding dimensionality (128-d) and controlled neighborhood expansion (3-hop) do not cause overfitting and, thus, are a promising and scalable solution for contemporary fraud detection system. This research connects the latest in GNN architectures and the real-world requirement for trustworthy consumer applications, while demonstrating the ability to defend against cyber threats proactively, interpretably, and with high performance.

all.title: LLM-CFExplainer: A Large Language Model-Guided Framework for Graph Counterfactual Explanations
all.venue: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering
all.abstract: Counterfactual explanations improve the interpretability of graph neural networks (GNNs) by identifying small structural or feature perturbations that alter model predictions. They are especially useful in applications sensitive to relational changes, including molecular property prediction, fraud detection, and recommendation systems. However, existing methods often rely on local importance scores or heuristic search, limiting their ability to capture global graph structure and generate prediction-relevant graph edits. We propose LLM-CFExplainer, a general framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to assist counterfactual generation for GNNs. The framework extracts neighborhood-level influence information from a trained GNN and converts it, together with the original graph information, into structured prompts. The LLM then performs relational reasoning and proposes counterfactual edits subject to prediction-flipping, domain consistency, and basic topological constraints. A lightweight verification module evaluates the validity of the proposed edits and ensures consistency with the original graph. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that LLM-CFExplainer improves counterfactual validity, coverage of perturbable regions, and coherence of generated explanations. These results demonstrate the potential of LLMs as reasoning tools for enhancing the interpretability of graph learning models. Our code is available at https://github.com/tanhaochen001-ux/LLM-CFExplainer .

all.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
all.abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune MLLMs with LoRA. Overall, the best MLLM reaches only 35.6% on the four-way T1 and catches far more video-only fakes than voice-only fakes (43.6% vs 7.5%). Trained detectors reach 98.4% on T1, and LoRA fine-tuning raises explanation scores (OmniVinci 4.17 to 7.40, Qwen2.5-Omni 4.42 to 6.98), but the best T1 detector falls to 78.3% when the face-swap generator is held out of training, so generalization and explanation remain open. We release the dataset, the compact MOZAIC-SMALL split, the code and the prompts.

all.title: Responsabilidade civil e inteligência artificial: os impactos dos deepfakes nos direitos da personalidade
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
institutions: Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro
all.abstract: RESUMO O presente trabalho analisa os impactos jurídicos da tecnologia deepfake sob as óticas da responsabilidade civil, dos reflexos penais, da tutela eleitoral e da proteção infantojuvenil no ambiente digital. Com a popularização da inteligência artificial generativa, a manipulação de imagem e de voz atingiu níveis de hiper-realismo que desafiam os institutos tradicionais de proteção à pessoa humana. O estudo investiga as ofensas aos direitos da personalidade, como imagem, honra e identidade pessoal, tangenciando o surgimento do dano existencial. Sob o prisma da responsabilidade civil, discute-se a imputação subjetiva aos criadores e a aplicação analógica do artigo 21 do Marco Civil da Internet para a remoção extrajudicial de conteúdos íntimos sintéticos por parte dos provedores. No âmbito penal, abordam-se os crimes contra a honra, o estelionato por clonagem de voz e o artigo 218-C do Código Penal. Ademais, examina-se a incidência do chamado "ECA Digital" (Lei nº 15.211/2025) na repressão à pornografia sintética de menores e na atribuição de responsabilidade civil solidária aos pais e instituições de ensino. Por fim, avalia-se o impacto dessas mídias na higidez do processo eleitoral frente às resoluções de rotulagem do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). Conclui-se que o ordenamento jurídico pátrio possui mecanismos dogmáticos suficientes para tutelar as vítimas, exigindo uma articulação coordenada e uma hermenêutica dinâmica entre as fontes cíveis, penais e constitucionais. Palavras-chave: Responsabilidade Civil. Deepfake. Direitos da Personalidade. Direito Penal. ECA Digital. Direito Eleitoral. ABSTRACT This article analyzes the legal impacts of deepfake technology from the perspectives of civil liability, criminal consequences, electoral protection, and child and adolescent safety in the digital environment. With the popularization of generative artificial intelligence, the manipulation of image and voice has reached hyper-realistic levels that challenge traditional frameworks of human dignity protection. The study investigates violations of personality rights, such as image, honor, and personal identity, characterizing the emergence of existential damage. From a civil liability standpoint, it discusses the subjective imputation of creators and the analogical application of Article 21 of the Brazilian Civil Rights Framework for the Internet (Marco Civil da Internet) for the extrajudicial removal of synthetic intimate content by application providers. In the criminal sphere, it addresses crimes against honor, fraud via voice cloning, and Article 218-C of the Criminal Code. Furthermore, the paper examines the impact of the "Digital Child and Adolescent Statute" (ECA Digita) in suppressing synthetic pornography involving minors and assigning joint civil liability to parents and educational institutions. Finally, it evaluates the impact of these synthetic media on the integrity of the electoral process in light of the labeling resolutions issued by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE). It concludes that the domestic legal order possesses sufficient dogmatic mechanisms to protect victims, requiring a coordinated articulation and dynamic hermeneutics among civil, criminal, and constitutional sources. Keywords: Civil Liability. Deepfake. Personality Rights. Criminal Law. Digital ECA. Electoral Law.

all.title: A PROTEÇÃO DA IMAGEM E DA HONRA NA ERA DIGITAL: UMA ANÁLISE DA RESPONSABILIDADE PREVENTIVA DAS PLATAFORMAS DIGITAIS FRENTE AS FRAUDES POR IA NO DIREITO BRASILEIRO
all.abstract: O presente artigo analisa a responsabilidade civil preventiva das plataformas digitais no ordenamento jurídico brasileiro, focando na tutela do direito à imagem e à honra diante do surgimento de conteúdos sintéticos gerados por Inteligência Artificial (deepfakes) e fraudes digitais. A pesquisa alcança o debate sobre a transição do modelo reativo do Marco Civil da Internet (Lei no 12.965/2014) para um dever de cuidado proativo e sistêmico, fundamentado no diálogo das fontes entre o Código de Defesa do Consumidor, o Código Civil e as diretrizes do Projeto de Lei no 2.338/2023 (Marco Legal da IA). Sustenta-se que a reparação posterior ao dano (ex post) tornou-se ineficaz e meramente simbólica em razão do caráter irreversível da exposição digital e da velocidade exponencial com que mídias manipuladas se proliferam no ciberespaço. O trabalho analisa de forma exaustiva a jurisprudência consolidada do Supremo Tribunal Federal fixada nos Temas no 987 e no 533 de Repercussão Geral, que reconheceram a inconstitucionalidade parcial e progressiva do artigo 19 do MCI, fixando critérios de responsabilidade solidária, regimes diferenciados de notificação extrajudicial e a exigência de deveres de cuidado e compliance algorítmico contra falhas sistêmica. Conclui-se que a imposição de salvaguardas técnicas preventivas tais como rotulagem algorítmica, marcas d'água criptográficas e detecção proativa consubstancia uma exigência imperativa para resguardar a dignidade da pessoa humana, os direitos da personalidade e a higidez do ambiente democrático.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence, Organizational Transformation, and the Rise of Organized Cybercrime as Non-State Digital Power
all.abstract: Most existing research continues to frame AI as a tactical instrument for phishing campaigns or deepfake fraud. That framing misses how these technologies are lowering barriers to entry, compressing innovation cycles, and producing networks that reconstitute faster than law enforcement can disrupt them. Drawing on peer-reviewed scholarship, primary-source criminal data, and threat assessments from Europol and Chainalysis covering 2022-2026, the chapter demonstrates why conventional disruption strategies continue to fall short and sketches what intelligence-led policing (ILP) and cross-border governance might require when the adversary can rebuild faster than enforcement can respond. The chapter contributes a conceptual framework that bridges criminology, organizational sociology, and the political economy of crime.

all.title: How Dangerous Can AI Be If Poorly Managed?
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This paper examines the potential harms of poorly managed artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on five major areas of risk: bias and discrimination, deepfake fraud and misinformation, cybersecurity threats, economic and social disruption, and loss of control over advanced AI systems. Using the International AI Safety Report 2026 as a framework, the paper reviews existing research, reports, and documented cases to distinguish between harms already observed in practice and risks that remain uncertain or have primarily been demonstrated in laboratory settings. The discussion highlights how inadequate data quality, insufficient testing, weak safeguards, and limited human oversight can increase the risks associated with AI deployment. It also examines layered approaches to AI risk management, including independent evaluations, technical safeguards, incident reporting, human oversight, public education, and adaptive regulation. The paper concludes that the consequences of AI depend not only on technological capabilities but also on how systems are designed, tested, deployed, and governed. Document type: Literature-based analytical review / preprint.

all.title: A RESPONSABILIZAÇÃO PENAL EM CRIMES MEDIADOS POR INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: DESAFIOS JURÍDICOS DIANTE DO USO DA IA COMO INSTRUMENTO DELITIVO
all.abstract: O avanço da Inteligência Artificial tem promovido transformações significativas na sociedade contemporânea, inclusive no modo como determinadas condutas criminosas são praticadas. Ferramentas baseadas em IA vêm sendo utilizadas para a execução de fraudes digitais, criação de conteúdos falsos (deepfakes) e manipulação de informações, ampliando a complexidade da atuação do Direito Penal. Nesse contexto, surge um problema central: o ordenamento jurídico penal brasileiro, estruturado a partir de conceitos clássicos do crime como dolo, culpa e autoria, demonstra-se suficiente para lidar com crimes mediados por Inteligência Artificial? Além disso, como se estabelece a responsabilização penal nesses casos — recaindo sobre o usuário, o desenvolvedor ou as empresas responsáveis pela tecnologia? O presente trabalho de conclusão de curso tem como objetivo analisar os desafios da tipificação e da responsabilização penal em condutas que envolvem o uso de IA como instrumento para a prática de crimes. A pesquisa pretende contribuir para o debate acerca da adequação do Direito Penal frente às novas tecnologias, bem como apontar possíveis caminhos interpretativos e regulatórios para o enfrentamento dessas novas formas de criminalidade.

all.title: Cochleogram-based ResNet-18 Network with Attention Mechanism (CoReA) for fake speech detection
Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
all.abstract: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. We evaluate it on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks, scoring every recording exactly as released, and against commercial systems on independent leaderboards. ARCAS 290M ranks first among all systems on the Podonos leaderboard and has the lowest equal error rate among commercial detectors on ASVspoof5. It separates real from AI-generated speech almost perfectly on ASVspoof5, SpeechFake, and ShiftySpeech, and detects nearly all AI-generated speech in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, and Telugu. On every benchmark with a published zero-shot comparison, including in-the-wild audio, partial fakes, and the conditions hardest for the field, it surpasses the strongest reported detector by a wide margin. These results establish ARCAS 290M as a general-purpose foundation for AI-generated audio detection in fraud prevention, platform safety, and media verification.

all.title: Sự cố 13/11/2026 và cảnh báo sớm cho an toàn: Hàng không, an ninh hạt nhân và ngân hàng trước phép thử mất Internet, mất AI và mất niềm tin vào dữ liệu
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: BẢN TIẾNG VIỆT: Tên tài liệu: Sự cố 13/11/2026 và cảnh báo sớm cho an toàn: Hàng không, an ninh hạt nhân và ngân hàng trước phép thử mất Internet, mất AI và mất niềm tin vào dữ liệuTác giả: S.S DUYMT, 2026 Tóm tắt nội dung:Công trình phân tích an toàn hệ thống và khả năng phục hồi hoạt động (operational resilience) này mổ xẻ một nghịch lý cấu trúc của thời đại số: các tổ chức không ngừng đầu tư để hệ thống và AI ra quyết định nhanh hơn, nhưng lại thường xuyên bỏ ngỏ việc xác định thời điểm và cơ chế để hệ thống buộc phải ngừng ra quyết định. Lấy điểm tựa thực nghiệm từ sự cố mạng viễn thông khiến Cục Hàng không Liên bang Mỹ (FAA) phải ban hành lệnh dừng cất cánh toàn quốc (ground stop) ngày 13/11/2026, tác giả chỉ ra bài học quản trị kép mang tính khuôn mẫu: năng lực an toàn tối thượng nằm ở khả năng đồng thời hạn chế rủi ro mới (ngăn máy bay mới cất cánh) và bảo toàn các nghĩa vụ đã phát sinh (đưa các chuyến bay đang ở trên trời hạ cánh an toàn bằng các kênh dự phòng độc lập). Từ bài học hàng không, nghiên cứu thiết lập một khung thẩm định toàn diện cho các hạ tầng trọng yếu quốc gia (Hàng không, Hạt nhân, Ngân hàng):• **Khung Khái niệm “Năng lực Dừng” (Stopping Capability):** Xác lập 4 thành tố bắt buộc để lệnh dừng không chỉ nằm trên giấy: Thẩm quyền được định trước $\to$ Tiêu chí kích hoạt rõ ràng $\to$ Kênh dữ liệu tin cậy độc lập $\to$ Chế độ vận hành suy giảm đã được diễn tập.• An ninh Hạt nhân và 5 Mặt của Tính Độc lập (IAEA): Cảnh báo nguy cơ khi đưa AI vào chuỗi điều khiển. Tác giả chỉ ra tính độc lập phải được bảo toàn trên cả 5 phương diện: dữ liệu, thiết bị/đường truyền, phần mềm/mô hình, tổ chức/con người và thời điểm thay đổi; đồng thời đề xuất phép thử “Tắt AI để thử con người” nhằm đối phó với “trớ trêu của tự động hóa”.• Khôi phục Trạng thái Giải trình được trong Ngân hàng (Basel): Phân tích rủi ro “khoản tiền đang bay” khi hệ thống thanh toán đứt gãy; tái định nghĩa đồng hồ phục hồi không tính bằng thời điểm máy chủ khởi động lại, mà tính bằng thời gian đưa toàn bộ giao dịch dở dang về trạng thái có thể đối soát và giải trình ($T_{\text{giải trình}} = T_{\text{phát hiện}} + T_{\text{cô lập}} + T_{\text{đối soát}} + T_{\text{thông tin}}$).• Bốn Phép Thử Căng Thẳng và Chuyển Đổi Mật Mã Hậu Lượng Tử (PQC): Thiết lập 4 bài diễn tập có tiêu chí chấm trượt (Tấn công mạo danh bằng AI, Mất Internet, AI ngừng hoặc trả lời sai, và Chuyển đổi PQC). Vận dụng bất đẳng thức Mosca ($X + Y > Z$) và các tiêu chuẩn NIST (FIPS 203, 204, 205; NIST IR 8547) cùng dự án BIS Project Leap để chứng minh: chuyển đổi mật mã phải bắt đầu từ tuổi thọ dữ liệu hôm nay để chặn đứng hiểm họa “Thu thập nay, giải mã sau”. Tiểu luận đúc kết 8 nguyên tắc chiến lược cùng bộ bài tập hành động cho hội đồng điều hành, khẳng định: “Một tổ chức an toàn không phải là tổ chức không bao giờ mất ổn định. Đó là tổ chức biết mình sẽ dừng ở đâu, giữ cái gì, và chứng minh được điều đó trước khi bị hỏi.” Đối tượng người đọc:• Hội đồng quản trị, Giám đốc Rủi ro (CRO), Giám đốc An toàn Thông tin (CISO) và lãnh đạo khối Hàng không, Năng lượng Hạt nhân, Ngân hàng• Cơ quan quản lý nhà nước, nhà hoạch định chính sách an ninh mạng và bảo vệ hạ tầng trọng yếu• Kiến trúc sư hệ thống, chuyên gia AI Safety, chuyên gia Mật mã hậu lượng tử và kiểm toán viên công nghệ Từ khóa (Keywords):Sự cố FAA 13/11/2026; An toàn hệ thống; Hạ tầng trọng yếu; Khả năng phục hồi hoạt động; Năng lực dừng; Phòng thủ theo chiều sâu; IAEA; Basel; Mật mã hậu lượng tử; PQC; Bất đẳng thức Mosca; Project Leap; AI Safety BẢN TIẾNG ANH (Zenodo English Abstract): Title: The Incident of November 13, 2026, and an Early Warning for System Safety: Aviation, Nuclear Security, and Banking Facing the Test of Lost Internet, Lost AI, and Lost Data TrustAuthor: S.S DUYMT, 2026 Abstract:This treatise investigates a profound systemic paradox in high-reliability organizations: the aggressive engineering of systems to make decisions faster while chronically neglecting the architectural mechanisms that dictate precisely when a system must cease automated decision-making. Grounded in the empirical natural experiment of the nationwide ground stop executed by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on November 13, 2026 due to telecommunication backbone instability, the author derives an essential dual-capability governance model: true operational resilience requires simultaneously halting the intake of new risk (grounding departures) while maintaining uncompromised, diverse channels to service in-flight commitments to completion (safely recovering airborne flights via analog radio and primary radar networks). Expanding beyond aviation, the monograph establishes an exhaustive operational resilience rubric across critical societal infrastructures:• The Four Pillars of "Stopping Capability": Formalizes the systemic architecture of safe halts: Predetermined Authority $\to$ Pre-established Trigger Criteria $\to$ Independent Out-of-Band Trust Channels $\to$ Rehearsed Degraded Operational Modes.• Nuclear Security and the Five Facets of Independence (IAEA): Evaluates the integration of AI within safety-critical architectures, proving that independence must hold across five distinct dimensions: data sources, physical infrastructure, software libraries, organizational reporting, and maintenance schedules. The author introduces the “AI-off” stress test to counteract Bainbridge’s classic "ironies of automation."• Financial Core and Indeterminate States (Basel Framework): Analyzes the systemic vulnerability of "in-flight transactions" during network decoupling. The metric of recovery is recalibrated from simple server reboot time to the comprehensive Time-to-Accountability ($T_{\text{accountability}} = T_{\text{detect}} + T_{\text{isolate}} + T_{\text{reconcile}} + T_{\text{inform}}$).• The Four Mandatory Stress Tests and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC): Establishes four rigorous simulation drills with explicit fail criteria: AI-assisted deepfake impersonation, total Internet outage, AI hallucination/shutdown, and PQC migration. Integrating Mosca’s Theorem ($X + Y > Z$) with NIST standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205; NIST IR 8547) and BIS Project Leap, the author demonstrates that cryptographic transitions must track data shelf-life today to mitigate the existential Harvest Now, Decrypt Later paradigm. The work culminates in eight strategic principles and actionable board-level exercises, establishing a timeless organizational maxim: “A safe organization is not one that never experiences instability. It is an organization that knows precisely where to halt, what core functions to preserve, and can empirically prove it before disaster strikes.” Target Audience:• Board members, Chief Risk Officers (CROs), and Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs) in Aviation, Nuclear Energy, and Banking• National regulatory bodies, critical infrastructure protection agencies, and homeland defense strategists• Enterprise system architects, AI safety researchers, post-quantum cryptographers, and disaster recovery coordinators Keywords:FAA Ground Stop 2026; System Safety; Critical Infrastructure; Operational Resilience; Stopping Capability; Defense-in-Depth; IAEA; Basel Committee; Post-Quantum Cryptography; PQC; Mosca's Inequality; Project Leap; AI Governance

all.title: BUILD OR DESTROY: A Critical Analysis of the Transformative Potential and Disinformation Risks of Modern Artificial Intelligence
all.abstract: OFFICIAL DESCRIPTION OF THE SCIENTIFIC WORK | INTERNATIONAL CATALOG 2026 RESEARCH TITLE: BUILD OR DESTROY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THE TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL AND DISINFORMATION RISKS OF MODERN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE LEAD RESEARCHER: Dr. Dieudelin Arcangel Legrand - Brotherswagg Robert Academic Jurisdiction and Country of Origin: Republic of Haiti PRIMARY PUBLISHING HOUSE: BrotherswaggStudioRecords Publishing (BSR Publishing) / TM3 MUSIC GROUP INSTITUTIONAL CORPORATE AUTHORSHIP, APPROVAL AND EDITORIAL REVIEW ENDORSEMENT: International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC) and its International Research Consortium: - The Hellenic Institute (Critical Thinking and Theoretical Frameworks) - The Atlantic Research Group (Factual Analysis and Global Perspective) - The Euro-Academic Council (Literary Standards and European Editorial Review) - The Oxbridge Academic (Methodological Rigor and Technical Review) - The Continental Bureau (Source Documentation and Multilingual Research) INTERNATIONAL EDITION: November 2026 ORIGINAL LANGUAGE OF PUBLICATION: Spanish (Official Master Edition) --- 1. SCIENTIFIC CLASSIFICATION AND EPISTEMOLOGICAL NATURE OF THE WORK This publication belongs to the genre of the Critical Review Scientific Article, Epistemological Analysis, and Technological Foresight (an In-Depth Argumentative Scientific Essay). By virtue of its interdisciplinary structure, the work is classified within the fields of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Philosophy of Technology, while establishing direct analytical connections with Communication Studies, Digital Sociology, Applied Ethics, Cognitive Psychology of Perception, and Cyber Law. Having undergone a rigorous process of methodological auditing and structural verification under the standards of the International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC), this research distinguishes itself from conventional technical literature through its comprehensive scope and unwavering commitment to empirical truth. It is neither a merely descriptive manual nor a speculative pamphlet, but rather a reference work designed to diagnose, with surgical precision, the most consequential technological phenomenon of our time. 2. WHY THIS WORK IS ESSENTIAL READING IN THE 21ST CENTURY Humanity is experiencing a historic moment in which the boundary between the real and the artificial has been erased by the speed of algorithms. Every day, millions of people interact with texts, voices, photographs, and video sequences that appear to reflect authentic events but have actually been entirely fabricated by generative artificial intelligence systems. Faced with this unprecedented reality, global society oscillates between two equally dangerous extremes: naïve fascination with the power of machines and uninformed panic in the face of a technology that few people fully understand. "Build or Destroy: A Critical Analysis of the Transformative Potential and Disinformation Risks of Modern Artificial Intelligence" was conceived to dispel this conceptual fog. This work confronts readers with an unavoidable question: How is it possible that the same technology capable of saving lives in medicine, accelerating scientific discoveries, and democratizing education has simultaneously become the preferred tool of countless digital content creators for falsifying reality, impersonating identities, and monetizing deception on a planetary scale? Through rigorous, direct, transparent prose, free from corporate constraints, the Lead Researcher, Dr. Dieudelin Arcangel Legrand - Brotherswagg Robert, together with the IIAEC collegiate body and BSR Publishing, exposes the hidden mechanisms behind this duality without barriers or concealment. Readers who explore these pages will encounter documented truths about how the attention economy operates, why digital platforms amplify synthetic falsehoods, and how society can defend its right to truth without renouncing scientific progress. 3. THE ARCHITECTURE OF THE WORK: AN EVOLUTIONARY NARRATIVE IN FOUR FOUNDATIONAL MODULES To provide a progressive, logical, and deeply enriching reading experience, this research has been structured into seven sections organized around four foundational modules that evolve as one continuous scientific narrative: - FIRST FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | Recent Evolution and Future Horizons of AI: Guides readers from the origins of symbolic computing to the transformer revolution, multimodal foundation models, and emerging autonomous agentic systems, clearly explaining how machines acquired the ability to synthesize realities indistinguishable from the physical world. - SECOND FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | The Constructive and Transformative Potential: Rigorously documents the positive side of this revolution, demonstrating how artificial intelligence is transforming medical diagnosis, drug design, climate sustainability, space research, the inclusion of persons with disabilities, and the democratization of knowledge in every corner of the planet. - THIRD FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | The Anatomy of Deception and a Critical Examination of Malicious Use: Constitutes the critical and revealing core of the manuscript. It examines with intellectual courage how numerous unscrupulous content creators exploit AI to manufacture deepfakes, clone human voices, fabricate pseudo-scientific or pseudo-journalistic evidence, and operate artificial engagement farms, thereby undermining the historical principle of audiovisual evidence and profiting from public credulity. - FOURTH FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | Ethical Discussion, Governance, and the Future of Trust: Proposes concrete solutions to the epistemic crisis by establishing the principles of mandatory transparency, cryptographic traceability from the point of origin, the legal shared responsibility of digital platforms, and the urgent need for critical literacy among citizens. 4. RELEVANCE TO UNIVERSITIES, RESEARCHERS, STUDENTS, AND SOCIETY This work has been conceived as an indispensable reference resource for multiple sectors of the global community: - For Researchers and Academics: It offers an interdisciplinary theoretical framework integrating algorithmic engineering, epistemology, and digital sociology, supported by cutting-edge technical references and international standards. - For Universities and Academic Institutions: It constitutes a bibliographic resource of significant educational value for courses in technological ethics, social communication, computer science, digital law, and contemporary philosophy. - For Students and Young Creators: It provides a moral and technical compass for understanding the power of the tools at their disposal, inspiring them to use artificial intelligence to build genuine knowledge and reject the culture of digital fraud. - For Citizens, Journalists, and the General Public: It delivers the practical and conceptual tools necessary to protect independent judgment against media manipulation and distinguish genuine progress from synthetic illusion. 5. A UNIVERSAL INVITATION: A WORK FOR EVERYONE, BREAKING DOWN BARRIERS AND BUILDING KNOWLEDGE WITHOUT BORDERS Beyond its methodological rigor and technical soundness, this research carries a fundamental declaration of principles: genuine scientific knowledge does not belong to closed elites or intellectual monopolies; it belongs to all humanity. For far too long, the production and validation of global knowledge have been concentrated within hermetic academic canons that erected invisible barriers—geographical, economic, linguistic, and racial—to determine who had the right to conduct research, publish, and be heard. all.title: A Set-Theoretic Tuple Model with Level-Consistent Normalization and Non-Compensatory Aggregation for Assessing the Cyber Resilience of Critical Infrastructure
institutions: State University of Information and Communication Technologies
State Scientific Institution "Institute of Information, Security and Law of the National Academy of Legal Sciences of Ukraine"
all.abstract: Cyber-resilience engineering frameworks organize protective activity into goals, objectives and basic actions but give no formal rules for turning heterogeneous security measurements into auditable scores. Building on earlier set-theoretic data and metric models of such a framework, this paper develops a set-theoretic tuple model for assessing the cyber resilience of critical infrastructure and analyzes, with proofs, the evaluation rules on which those models relied. The hierarchy of the Cyber Resiliency Engineering Framework is encoded as an indexed family of sets with an injective identifier map; admissible threat-scenario projections form a finite distributive lattice; and each basic action carries a tuple of metrics. A clipped affine normalization agrees with a five-level class table if and only if the gaps between class boundaries are proportional to those between score breakpoints, and the two-threshold rule of the earlier models is consistent with no table; an anchored piecewise-linear normalization is consistent by construction. A capped knockout operator, which keeps a missing critical capability from being offset by other metrics, retains veto, idempotency and continuity in the normalized scores, whereas neither the hard gate nor power discounting has all three. In an illustrative bank phishing scenario, 9 of 38 observed metrics receive a linear score outside their tabulated level, and the threat-intelligence action moves from high (0.903) to above average (0.856). A parameter study shows how the cap threshold, the weights and the choice of core metrics affect the verdicts. Constructed degraded states activate the cap, the operator is compared with the geometric and harmonic means and the minimum, and a randomized check of the formal rules over 100,000 synthetic states shows that the effects are not peculiar to the example; it does not validate the policy parameters. The model is a formal scoring method that turns heterogeneous security evidence into reproducible, auditable scores; its rules are mathematically valid, but it has not been validated against expert judgment or field data, and no operational or predictive validity under an adversary is claimed.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Password Cracking in E-Learning Systems: A Systematic Review, Hierarchical Taxonomy of Underlying Algorithms, and Evidence-Based Mitigation Strategies
all.venue: Iraqi Journal of Information and Technology Systems
all.abstract: The embrace of e-learning has raised the cybersecurity risk levels of education systems, especially with the advent of AI for faster password-guessing attacks. This review aimed to fill the gap in security research in e-learning environments by focusing on the use of AI to crack passwords. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 42 studies published between 2021 and 2025 were identified from seven databases, and 12 seminal works were added through citation searching. The review provides a taxonomy of the AI cracking techniques, a framework of the complete attack lifecycle, an evidence map of datasets and performance metrics, and a research roadmap. Half of the reviewed studies were published in 2025, and only 14.3% implement a password-generation model. No single AI architecture consistently outperforms the others; effective protection therefore requires a combination of multi-factor authentication, behavioral biometrics, adaptive access control and phishing-resistant passwordless authentication.

all.title: THE CHURCH IS A SCAM": WHY DO PEOPLE SAY SO, AND HOW DID WE GET HERE
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The phrase "the church is a scam" describes Nigerian churches' growing reputation for fraud. It examines how financial mismanagement, sexual immorality, erroneous prophecies, hypocrisy, and other church issues damage trust. Social and traditional media scandals are weakening Christianity's effect on Nigeria's morality and society. The mixed-methods study used quantitative and qualitative data to explain these impressions. Researchers surveyed 356,100 Nigerians in 14 Christian-oriented states in person and via Google Forms. In the qualitative component, 24 key informant interviews and 8 focus group discussions (FGDs) with 46,000 participants were used to explore personal and social narratives that undermine church credibility. Quantitative data analysis included descriptive statistics, bivariate analysis, and multiple regression, whereas qualitative data were analysed using NVIVO theme analysis. Research shows that financial malfeasance, sexual impropriety, and hypocrisy lead to a perception of church fraud. Many say religious leaders profit from their followers while living in luxury. The media is necessary because viral videos, digital conversations, and investigative journalism breed scepticism. Younger, more educated people are more critical in these evaluations. However, financially transparent and accountable churches are trusted. The study recommends ethical church leaders, transparent financial management, congregants' engagement in financial and administrative choices, and independent monitoring bodies to review church funds. Churches must own up to their fault, compensate victims, and put gospel-centered missions before consumerism. The media and public must be accountable to rebuild trust. This study examines religion, trust, and accountability. It advises Nigerian and international religious organisations on restoring integrity, transparency, and public trust in the church's moral authority.

all.title: Vitiated Consent Beyond the Courts: Seeking Redress for Coerced Debt through the Australian Financial Complaints Authority
all.abstract: In this article we consider the possibility of relief from coerced debt — arising where a borrower or guarantor’s consent to assume financial obligations was the result of coercion by an intimate partner. Equity and statute may provide grounds for relief where consent was vitiated by coercion, pressure or fraud in the context of economic abuse. Yet victim-survivors seeking release from liability for coerced debt in court face multiple barriers and low chances of success. The prohibitive cost of litigation means victim-survivors are more likely to seek redress through lenders’ internal dispute resolution processes, or through the ombudsman service provided by the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (‘AFCA’). We examine the findings of a ‘case review’ of AFCA determinations where complainants sought release from liability or compensation for coerced debt. Although AFCA represents a more accessible and less legalistic forum than the courts, we show that, at its determination stage, the substantive barriers faced by victim-survivors arguing equitable and statutory vitiated consent grounds can be similar to those that have arisen in court. AFCA’s current approach to coerced debt also gives lenders limited incentive to identify, document and respond to the dynamics that lead to such contracts when approving transactions — potentially resulting in missed opportunities to prevent coerced debt at the outset.

all.title: Effectiveness Of Handling General Criminal Offenses By The Criminal Investigation Unit Of Jembrana Police Department, Bali Regional Police
all.abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of online fraud case handling by the Criminal Investigation Unit of the Jembrana Resort Police, Bali Regional Police, within its broader mandate to investigate general criminal offenses. An empirical socio-legal approach with a qualitative descriptive design was employed, incorporating interviews, observations, document analysis, and administrative records covering 2022–2025. The findings included statements from four police officers, although the total number of informants was not specified. The number of newly reported fraud cases declined from 24 in 2022 to 20 in 2023, seven in 2024, and three in 2025, while recorded case closures totaled 19, 24, eight, and three, respectively. The annual case closure-to-intake ratios exceeded 100% in 2023 and 2024, suggesting that some closures may have involved cases carried over from previous years. However, these aggregate figures did not establish cohort-specific resolution rates or demonstrate improvements in investigation speed without case-level data. Administrative records also indicated increased participation in cybercrime investigation training, while interviewed officers emphasized the importance of timely crime reporting, digital evidence preservation, and coordination with financial institutions and specialized police units. The principal challenges included inadequate digital forensic facilities, disparities in investigators' technical competencies, delayed reporting by victims, and perpetrators' use of fraudulent identities and anonymous online accounts. Public satisfaction summaries indicated generally favorable perceptions of police services, although the underlying sampling procedures and measurement methods remained unclear. The study contributed an integrated assessment of administrative performance indicators, investigative practices, and public service quality in handling online fraud cases. The findings highlighted the need to strengthen digital forensic investigation capabilities, standardize case monitoring and documentation procedures, improve communication with victims, and establish verifiable performance indicators to assess investigative effectiveness and case resolution outcomes.

all.title: PropTrust Association Institutional Dossier & PTVS v2.0 Specification: The Autonomous Physical Oracle for Institutional RWA Tokenization
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: OverviewThis document serves as the official institutional dossier and technical specification for the Prop Trust Verified Standard (PTVS v2.0), developed and governed by the PropTrust Association (Zug, Switzerland). It establishes the definitive framework for resolving the "Physical Oracle Gap" in Real-World Asset (RWA) tokenization, bridging the disconnect between blockchain immutability and physical reality. Core Architecture: The Four ModulesPTVS v2.0 transforms inert physical assets into live, programmable financial entities through four normative extensions: RFC-004 (Hardware-Attested Edge Capture): Eliminates document fraud via Secure Enclave mobile capture, Galileo OSNMA geolocation, and eIDAS 2.0 Qualified Electronic Signatures. RFC-005 (Privacy-Preserving Planetary Telemetry): Enables continuous InSAR satellite monitoring processed in AMD SEV-SNP confidential enclaves (Google Cloud) without revealing asset locations. RFC-006 (Zero-Knowledge Solvency Vaults): Utilizes ZK-SNARKs to prove physical and legal solvency to regulators and banks without compromising institutional privacy. RFC-007 (Dynamic Risk & Parametric Escrow): Introduces the Physical Integrity Index ($I_{fis}$), automatically adjusting collateral haircuts and releasing funds via smart contracts based on real-time physical state. Governance & Regulatory AlignmentThe standard is governed by the PropTrust Association, a Swiss Verein ensuring neutral, decentralized oversight. The architecture is natively aligned with MiCA (EU 2023/1114), Basel III (SCO60), and eIDAS 2.0, providing a compliant infrastructure for institutional adoption. Organizational Structure and Governance Model (Three-Chamber System). Academic References and Persistent Identifiers (DOIs). License & AvailabilityThe technical documentation is available under CC BY 4.0. The smart contract code is available under BUSL-1.1 at github.com/aurema-group/ptvs-rwa-oracle. all.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models for Automation and Smart Manufacturing in Production and Service Industries
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding and transforming the industrial and service industries. This is leading to a shift to automation and intelligent manufacturing. The 4.0 industry has established a digitally connected world where machines, human beings, and processes work harmoniously. AI and LLMs are crucial to this paradigm, and they can be used alongside automation technologies, robotics, and data-driven decisions to help organizations predict demand, optimize schedules, and minimize downtimes. LLMs augment the management of knowledge, create technical documentation, and provide a gap in communication between human operators and complex systems. They are applied to generative AI to assist in designing smart products, make the supply chain logistics more efficient, and provide real-time quality control with the help of computer vision and reinforcement learning. The AI-powered cobots and voice-based systems have empowered human employees in the workplace, building cooperative workplaces with safety and efficiency coexisting. These intelligent chatbots, voice assistants, and automated response systems will provide 24/7 customer service in high levels of personalization. LLMs are used in the healthcare sector in diagnostics, treatment planning, and patient record management, whereas AI predictive care and medical imaging are improved by AI. Financial services are beneficiaries of real-time fraud detection, compliance, and automated advisory systems, and as a result, smart ecosystems with distributed decision-making across cloud and edge platforms are formed, allowing them to be responsive in real time. However, large-scale applications come with their own set of big problems, including the risks of data security breaches, significant costs of implementation, worker retraining, and ethical concerns of autonomous factories, hyper-personalized service experiences, and energy-efficient production systems that would be consistent with sustainability efforts. The breakthroughs in quantum computing and edge AI are set to enhance the speed of decision-making processes whereas the human-centered AI design will make it more inclusive and trustworthy .

all.title: Game-based learning in financial education and implications for financial criminology pedagogy: A systematic literature review
all.abstract: This systematic literature review examines game-based learning (GBL) interventions in financial education and their implications for financial criminology pedagogy. Twenty-eight peer-reviewed studies published between January 2015 and March 2026 were identified through five databases in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). The review addresses the scope and nature of GBL interventions in financial education (RQ1), their effectiveness (RQ2) and how they can inform financial criminology pedagogy (RQ3). RQ1 and RQ2 were addressed through narrative synthesis; RQ3 is a conceptual extrapolation from that evidence, supplemented by literature on GBL in cybersecurity education, because few studies address financial crime directly. The interventions comprised digital games, board games, gamified applications, simulations and generative-AI-assisted designs, delivered mainly to school and university learners in 15 countries and one multi-country European study. Most studies with comparison groups, including a multi-country randomised trial, reported gains in financial knowledge, and several reported improved motivation or engagement, although many had important design limitations. Evidence of change in real-world financial behaviour was weak: most outcomes were measured at the end of the intervention, often by self-report, and few studies reported follow-up. Only one included study concerned financial crime directly: a survey of university students’ willingness to use a proposed anti-fraud game, which did not evaluate learning. The review therefore offers evidence-informed propositions for GBL in financial criminology education, namely consequential decision-making, structured debriefing, adaptive feedback and the simulation of deception and information asymmetry, which require direct empirical testing.

all.title: The emerging role of artificial intelligence in financial and management accounting: insights from a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
all.abstract: Purpose This study addresses the fragmentation of research on artificial intelligence (AI) in financial and management accounting through a bibliometric examination of the literature, at a time when AI is reshaping reporting timeliness, audit quality, fraud detection and managerial decision-making while raising governance and explainability risks that current disclosure and assurance frameworks were not designed to address. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a systematic literature review combined with bibliometric analysis, drawing on 245 peer-reviewed articles indexed in the Scopus database over the period 1985–2026. Following PRISMA guidelines, performance analysis and science-mapping techniques are applied using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. Findings The keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies six thematic clusters: AI as a methodological umbrella; core enablers like machine learning and big data; AI-enabled financial decision support for small and medium-sized enterprises; advanced analytics in finance and forecasting; AI-enabled risk and organisational forecasting; and technical foundations of AI-driven risk assessment. The bibliographic coupling identifies six document clusters spanning fraud detection, neural network applications, management accounting, digital transformation, financial distress/credit risk and AI ethics/governance. Machine learning, financial management and risk assessment are basic themes near the motor-theme boundary, while financial accounting sits in the emerging/declining quadrant. The field moves from expert systems (1985–2010) through machine learning/analytics (2011–2020) to AI governance and ethical accountability (2021–2026). Research limitations/implications The analysis is restricted to Scopus-indexed, peer-reviewed journal articles, excluding Web of Science, conference proceedings and practitioner reports. As a bibliometric study, the methods identify structural patterns and intellectual trends but cannot assess causal mechanisms, qualitative depth or implementation-level outcomes, and the post-2023 rise of generative AI means the snapshot will need periodic updating. Future research should employ empirical, longitudinal and mixed-methods designs to examine the organisational, contextual and ethical implications of AI adoption across diverse accounting environments and regulatory settings. Practical implications These findings are relevant for accounting professionals, managers, auditors, educators and regulators involved in both internal management processes and external financial reporting. By systematically mapping the evolution and thematic structure of AI in financial and management accounting, the study shows how AI tools enhance reporting timeliness, analytical depth and decision usefulness while raising concerns related to transparency, explainability and governance. The results can support accounting educators in curriculum redesign, assist practitioners in aligning AI adoption with reporting objectives and inform regulators in revisiting disclosure requirements, assurance frameworks and internal controls. Originality/value The study examines AI jointly across financial and management accounting, extends coverage to 2026 and proposes a governance-anchored three-layer framework grounded in the resource-based view and socio-technical systems theory.

all.title: Agentic AI in Finance
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This working paper examines how agentic AI (systems that plan, call tools, retain state and act within defined constraints) is being applied across financial services, and what it takes to deploy it responsibly. Ten chapters cover the shift from generative to agentic AI; the building blocks of agentic systems (agent architectures, large language models and reasoning, tools, memory, orchestration and knowledge graphs); customer-facing agents in retail banking; fraud, compliance and risk management; investment management and capital markets; operations and back-office transformation; building, deploying and scaling agents; the regulatory landscape and ethical guardrails; case studies and lessons learned; and the outlook for the coming decade. The case studies include the authors' own prototypes: an agentic Monte Carlo Value-at-Risk simulator, a cross-jurisdiction regulatory comparison tool and a continuous policy gap-analysis loop. First drafted in 2025, the paper was reviewed and updated in November 2026. Statistics, case studies and statements about law and regulation were checked against current sources (position as of 13 November 2026), and external claims that could be traced are tied to a numbered list of 62 references. A Review and Update Note sets out what was corrected and added. Nothing in this paper is legal, regulatory or investment advice.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence and Automation in Finance and Accounting Processes: Part 2
all.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
all.abstract: AI and automation are reshaping finance and accounting by changing how financial information is captured, processed, analysed, controlled and communicated. Machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, robotic process automation and generative AI increasingly support activities ranging from invoice processing and reconciliation to auditing, fraud detection, forecasting and management decision support. These technologies can improve speed, consistency and analytical capacity, but their value depends on data quality, system integration, professional oversight and responsible governance. Their adoption also creates material risks concerning confidentiality, cybersecurity, explainability, bias, accountability and workforce readiness. This chapter provides a critical synthesis of AI and automation across the finance and accounting lifecycle. It explains the principal technologies, examines operational and strategic applications, evaluates organisational benefits and limitations, and develops a governance-oriented view of future intelligent finance.
